title: SNE Research: Chinese OEMs increasingly dominate global EV battery market - electrive.com
content:
In the first nine months of this year, Chinese manufacturers secured more than half of the battery market for electric and hybrid vehicles outside China - while Korean and Japanese suppliers lost ground. This is according to a new analysis by SNE Research.
Image: Cora Werwitzke
South Korean market research firm SNE Research has analysed the dynamics and market share distribution of the EV battery market outside China. The key finding: the total capacity of these batteries climbed to 426.7 GWh from January to September. The market thus grew by 24.7 per cent compared to the same period the previous year. The clear beneficiaries are Chinese battery manufacturers.
“The combined market share of the six Chinese companies, including [CATL, BYD, Gotion, SVOLT, CALB and EVE] rose 13.3 per cent from 43.1 to 56.4 per cent, exceeding half of the non-China market,” writes SNE Research. CATL and BYD alone account for 44.5 per cent of the market. In the same period in 2023, this figure was still 36.7 per cent.
SNE Research specifically analysed the sales of batteries for battery-electric vehicles (BEVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), and other hybrids, highlighting that regional demand developed differently. The Korean analysts note that demand in Europe and Asia compensated for the ongoing weakness in North America. Interestingly, China itself also appears to be faltering. While SNE Research certifies 24.7 per cent growth for the global market excluding China, the increase including China is only 19.7 per cent. Overall momentum is thus slowing in the People’s Republic.
The following figures are available for the manufacturers themselves: The three Korean manufacturers – LG Energy Solution, SK On and Samsung SDI – contributed a total of 113.0 GWh worldwide (excluding China) from January to September, a decline of 13.5 per cent compared to the previous year. Their combined market share fell sharply by 11.7 percentage points, from 38.2 per cent to 26.5 per cent. According to SNE Research, business in North America crumbled in particular, where the installed battery capacity of the trio nearly halved from 56.1 to 28.1 GWh. In Europe, however, there was a slight increase (from 58.7 to 63.0 GWh), as well as in Asia (from 13.1 to 17.5 GWh).
But let’s take it step by step. After the first nine months, CATL once again leads the ranking. Outside China, the company achieved a volume of 143.7 GWh, which corresponds to exactly one-third of the market. Compared to the previous year, CATL grew by 47 per cent. Its market share increased by 5.1 percentage points to 33.7 per cent. For Europe, SNE Research statistics show a 35 per cent increase from 71.5 to 96.8 GWh, while in Asia, the volume doubled to 27.1 GWh.
Table: SNE Research
According to the analysts,
LG Energy Solution
maintains second place with 69.8 GWh (-4.9 per cent year-over-year). Its business in Europe and Asia developed positively. In Europe, it increased by 13 per cent to 38.6 GWh, and in Asia by 49 per cent to 11.1 GWh. However, this was not enough to offset the sharp decline in North America (-45 per cent year-over-year, from 29.9 to 16.5 GWh). LGES’s market share fell significantly by 5.1 percentage points, from 21.5 per cent to 16.4 per cent.
Next is BYD – with 45.9 GWh (+67 per cent year-over-year) – in third place. The company’s market share grew from 8.0 per cent to 10.8 per cent. According to SNE Research, this growth was distributed across Europe (17.4 GWh, +67 per cent year-over-year), Asia (14.8 GWh, +41 per cent year-over-year) and South America (7.1 GWh, +136 per cent year-over-year).
Panasonic ranks fourth after the first nine months of the year with 35.6 GWh (-0.8 per cent year-over-year). “Tesla’s North American volumes supported its results, but growth fell well short of the non-China market,” the authors said. Panasonic’s market share fell by 2.1 percentage points to 8.4 per cent. Looking further back, Panasonic’s example particularly illustrates how much the market has changed in recent years:
Meanwhile, SK On in fifth place recorded significant losses, with its volume dropping to 28.2 GWh (-18 per cent year-over-year). Its market share plummeted from 10.0% to 6.6 per cent. “The company supplies batteries to Hyundai Motor Group, Ford, Volkswagen, and Mercedes-Benz, among others, but its usage declined 46.7 per cent in North America and 2.2 per cent in Europe,” the study states.
VW partner Gotion grew by 153.8 per cent to 17.6 GWh, thereby overtaking Samsung SDI, which slipped to seventh place. Samsung SDI recorded only 15.0 GWh (-34.4 per cent year-over-year) – the sharpest decline among the top 10. Its market share fell from 6.7 per cent to 3.5 per cent. While sales in Europe remained stable at 9.4 GWh, Samsung SDI experienced a debacle in North America (-66 per cent year-over-year, from 12.0 to 4.1 GWh).
The top 10 is rounded out by three second-tier Chinese suppliers – namely SVOLT, CALB and EVE Energy. SVOLT grew by 102 per cent to 13.1 GWh, CALB by 88.5 per cent to 10.6 GWh, and EVE Energy achieved a massive increase of 215 per cent to 9.5 GWh.
In summary, it can be concluded that the three Korean manufacturers and Panasonic each had to cede market share in the global market excluding China, while the six mentioned Chinese companies consistently and rapidly expanded their volume in Europe. A major factor here is cell chemistry: “The LFP share of the non-China market rising 11.9 per cent from 15.8 per cent to 27.7 per cent reflects the same trend. In North America,” the SNE research analysts stated. This is because it is primarily Chinese manufacturers that are leading the way in LFP technology. In Europe, the adoption of LFP is increasing – “mainly in entry-level models, making price competitiveness a key criterion in supplier selection,” they added.
Based on the data, the study’s authors believe that regional political frameworks and the diversification of demand will primarily determine the competitiveness of suppliers. Some manufacturers are now increasingly shifting to batteries for stationary storage to achieve greater diversification – particularly in North America. With regard to Europe, the analysts consider the Auto Package and the associated incentive of the so-called combustion engine phase-out, as well as potential ‘Made-in-Europe’ rules, to be a decisive influencing factor.

title: Campine boosts antimony market grip with Thai stake – Batteries International
content: European lead and metals recycler Campine is to acquire a minority stake in the manufacturing operations of Thai antimony smelting and trading firm Green Tech Antimony. Campine said on November 3 the undisclosed investment marks a major step in its speciality chemicals plans and gives it access to an Asian production base for antimony trioxide (ATO) — strengthening the supply chain for its Belgium-based operations and opening new opportunities in global markets. Green Tech Antimony operates a smelter at Kanchanaburi, commissioned in 2025, with an annual production capacity of 8,000 tonnes of antimony metal. The company’s Thai partners also own several antimony mines in Southeast Asia, providing access to ore concentrates. By the end of 2027, Kanchanaburi will be expanded with a 4,000-tonne ATO production unit using Campine’s proprietary technology, creating an integrated operation from antimony ore to finished ATO. The entire ATO output will be marketed through a new trading company, majority-controlled by Campine, primarily targeting Asian markets. The deal, expected to be finalised in January 2027, follows Campine’s pledge in January 2026 to invest €7 million ($8 million) in an expansion of its proprietary antimony recycling technology, following its acquisition of two battery recycling plants and one semi-finished lead-products facility from Ecobat in France. The strategic importance of antimony to a wide range of sectors — including batteries and solar panels and for defence and advanced manufacturing applications — has grown amid global supply chain disruptions and China’s export restrictions on antimony-related products. Campine said it became the global market leader in ATO in early 2025, following exceptional supply disruptions and sharp price increases. Since the end of 2025, improved raw material availability has led to a significant correction in antimony prices. content: A new blueprint to guide industry and academia partnerships in developing next-gen battery technologies in America has been launched by the federal government. The US energy department’s Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation unveiled its strategy for American leadership in batteries on October 27 — alongside the Battery Manufacturing Accelerator (BattMan) Consortium, led by the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL), The strategy set out the energy department’s priorities to build a fully integrated domestic battery supply chain by 2030, achieve “US leadership in battery technology and manufacturing by 2035”, and accelerate the commercialisation of safe, affordable, and reliable energy-storage solutions. Meanwhile, BattMan will focus on lowering manufacturing costs, speeding the transition of novel battery technologies from laboratory discovery to manufacturing deployment, and boosting US leadership in energy storage manufacturing. PNNL is a member of Battery Council International, which praised the US national lab’s work in connecting other national labs, industry and universities on next-gen battery technologies. “BCI applauds these efforts that line up closely with what our members do every day,” the trade body said. BattMan will harness super intelligence and advanced manufacturing capabilities to identify challenges earlier and improve production processes. The accelerator will also strengthen critical mineral supply chains by advancing battery materials made from more abundant domestic elements. Assistant US energy secretary Audrey Robertson said: “The advances we make today in battery manufacturing technology will determine America’s energy security and economic competitiveness for decades to come. “The Battery Manufacturing Accelerator will fast track commercialisation, strengthen domestic supply chains and help ensure that innovative domestic manufacturing is used for the next generation of battery technologies.” PNNL won BCI’s annual innovation award in 2025 for its Grid Storage Launchpad, a new US national capability for speeding up energy storage research. Also last year, BCI hosted the inaugural Flow Batteries North America conference in partnership with PNNL. Earlier this year, South Korea’s Energy Tech Solution installed a prismatic battery assembly line at PNNL. title: EnerSys in $320m take-over of Ultralife – Batteries International
content: EnerSys is to take over New York-based battery tech company Ultralife in a $320 million enterprise value acquisition. The lead and lithium manufacturer said on October 27 the deal expands its presence in advanced, differentiated battery technologies with US-based manufacturing. EnerSys expects to realise $15 million to $20 million in annual run-rate cost synergies within the first 18 months. Ultralife, which also has operations in Canada, the UK and China, is a leading provider of rechargeable and non-rechargeable batteries, battery systems, and related accessories for military communications and other specialised applications. The transaction, expected to close in the first quarter of calendar 2027, will be funded through cash on hand. EnerSys president and CEO Shawn O’Connell said: “Building on the success of our recent acquisitions, Ultralife expands our portfolio of advanced, reliable, high-performance power solutions. Together, we will be better positioned to support the US Department of War and allied forces with leading-edge, cost-effective technologies for the increasingly electrified battlefield of the future.” Batteries International reported in July 2026 that EnerSys had refocused plans for its $500 million battery cell gigafactory in South Carolina for US defence needs — and was ending a tech partnership with French Li cells developer Verkor. The move came after EnerSys announced a realignment of its previous four operating units into a three-segment operating model. title: Solid Power Announces Significant Advancement in Commercial Pathway, Commissioning MOBIUS™ Continuous Electrolyte Manufacturing Line - Batteries News
content:
Solid Power Announces Significant Advancement in Commercial Pathway, Commissioning MOBIUS™ Continuous Electrolyte Manufacturing Line
Continuous manufacturing pilot line for sulfide-based solid electrolyte designed to increase Solid Power’s annual electrolyte production capacity at Thornton, Colorado facility by 150%.
Commissioning of MOBIUS™ is underway following substantial completion of construction with materials now being introduced into the line.
Advances Solid Power toward continuous production, which will support commercial readiness and potential cost curve advancements.
Primary powder processing site acceptance testing (SAT) is complete. Full SAT is expected by the end of the month, and operational startup is planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.
LOUISVILLE, Colo.–(BUSINESS WIRE)–Solid Power, Inc. (Nasdaq: SLDP), a leading U.S.-based developer of solid-state battery technology, today announced that it has begun commissioning MOBIUS™, its continuous manufacturing pilot line for sulfide-based solid electrolyte. Previously referred to as the SP2.5 Continuous Manufacturing Pilot Line, MOBIUS™ has reached substantial completion of construction at Solid Power’s SP2 facility in Thornton, Colorado, and materials are now being introduced into the line. MOBIUS™ supports Solid Power’s objective to manufacture and sell electrolyte to Tier 1 battery manufacturers and automotive original equipment manufacturers (OEMs).
John Van Scoter,
President and Chief Executive Officer of Solid Power, Inc, said:
Bringing the promise of MOBIUS™ to fruition is a proud moment for our team and a critical step in positioning Solid Power for commercial readiness and long-term stockholder value creation,
“The name MOBIUS™ reflects what sets this line apart: continuous production designed to deliver the process control, repeatability, and scale our partners expect from a commercial electrolyte supplier. With MOBIUS™, we expect to increase our electrolyte production capacity at SP2 in Thornton, Colorado, by 150%, and we look forward to bringing the line into full operation and supporting material qualification with our partners.”
Solid Power has also completed SAT for primary powder processing on MOBIUS™ and expects to complete full SAT by the end of October 2026. SAT is an activity performed with Solid Power and the equipment manufacturer in parallel to confirm that the equipment works as specified and designed before progressing into production. With commissioning underway, Solid Power continues to work toward plant validation and operational startup, which remain planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.
MOBIUS™ is designed to add 45 metric tons of solid electrolyte production capacity per year. Following commissioning, total electrolyte production capacity at the SP2 facility is expected to reach approximately 75 metric tons per year. MOBIUS™ will operate alongside the facility’s existing batch production lines, using what Solid Power believes is the world’s first continuous manufacturing process for sulfide-based solid electrolyte.
MOBIUS™ plays a central role in Solid Power’s commercial readiness. Solid Power believes continuous manufacturing is fundamental to achieving the volume, consistency, and cost required for commercial electrolyte supply, and expects continuous production to deliver tighter process control and more consistent output than batch processing. MOBIUS™ will also support material qualification with automotive and cell manufacturing partners as Solid Power advances toward commercial electrolyte supply.
MOBIUS™ was built as part of a project supported by the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) through an assistance agreement providing up to $50 million in federal funding.

title: Samsung SDI and Alpha Omega Power Sign 1 GWh Supply Agreement for US-Made Energy Storage - Batteries News

Samsung SDI and Alpha Omega Power Sign 1 GWh Supply Agreement for US-Made Energy Storage
Supply deals with AOP totaling 1.5 GWh, with all products to be manufactured at the SPE plant in Indiana
SBB 1.7 features high-nickel NCA prismatic batteries and proven fire safety, supporting AOP projects in the WECC and ERCOT power markets
Samsung SDI expands its North American ESS presence as AOP grows its U.S. storage portfolio
HOUSTON & SEOUL, Korea–(BUSINESS WIRE)–Samsung SDI today announced that its Michigan-based subsidiary, Samsung SDI America (SDIA), has signed a 1 GWh agreement to supply energy storage system (ESS) solutions to Alpha Omega Power (AOP), a U.S. utility-scale battery storage developer and independent power producer. Including an initial contract signed late last year, the two agreements total 1.5 GWh.
AOP plans to deploy the ESS solutions supplied by Samsung SDI for large-scale power projects critical for grid reliability and power demand growth, scheduled to begin construction in the WECC and ERCOT power markets next year.
Under the latest agreement, Samsung SDI will supply its Samsung Battery Box (SBB) 1.7, a fully integrated ESS solution featuring nickel cobalt aluminum (NCA) batteries. All cells and modules will be manufactured at the StarPlus Energy (SPE) plant in Kokomo, Indiana, and delivered by the end of this year.
SBB 1.7 features high-capacity, high-nickel NCA chemistry and delivers 17% higher energy density than its predecessor, SBB 1.5, while maintaining the same 20-foot footprint. The solution also incorporates Samsung SDI’s ESS design expertise, including AI-powered algorithms for early anomaly detection and battery life prediction, and is designed for 25 years of continuous use.
SBB 1.7 has also obtained certifications and met safety standards including NFPA 855, the National Fire Protection Association’s standard for the installation of stationary energy storage systems, and UL 9540, a safety standard for ESS. The solution also incorporates Samsung SDI’s proprietary Enhanced Direct Injection (EDI) technology, which directly injects fire-extinguishing agents into individual battery modules, further enhancing fire safety.
Samsung SDI has secured a series of ESS supply deals with U.S. energy companies this year and continues to discuss potential supply agreements with a number of local customers, with additional orders expected in the near future.
Industry analysts attribute Samsung SDI’s recent contract wins in part to its prismatic battery technology (PrismStack), known for its strong performance and safety.
Samsung SDI is currently the only non-Chinese supplier of prismatic ESS batteries in North America. With strong durability and fire safety compared with pouch-type batteries, its prismatic batteries have helped the company meet the stringent requirements of U.S. energy companies.
Paul Choi,
CEO of Alpha Omega Power, said:
American-made ESS from Samsung SDI will play an important role in AOP’s continued growth,
“This second agreement strengthens our domestic supply chain supporting the next generation of energy infrastructure.”
Fabrice Hudry,
President ESS, Samsung SDI America (SDIA), said:
Alpha Omega Power is one of the fastest growing independent power producers in the country, and the kind of sophisticated operator we want to partner with to tackle grid reliability challenges,
“With our differentiated technology and local production capabilities, we will continue to expand our business foundation and strengthen our position in the North American ESS market.”

title: Amorphous carbon coatings for longer-lasting lithium-metal batteries - Batteries News
content:
Amorphous carbon coatings for longer-lasting lithium-metal batteries
The demand for more powerful and lighter battery systems is growing. Batteries with high energy density and long service life are in high demand, particularly for electric mobility, aerospace, and stationary energy storage. The Fraunhofer Institute for Surface Engineering and Thin Films IST is therefore collaborating with the Fraunhofer USA Center Midwest (CMW) to explore new approaches for improving the performance and service life of future battery systems. One promising approach involves lithium-metal anodes, in which lithium itself serves as the active anode material; due to its high specific capacity, this enables battery cells with potentially higher energy density.
To harness the potential of lithium-metal anodes for longer-lasting battery cells, the new research project “LIMAC – Amorphous Carbon Interlayers for Reliable Lithium-Metal Battery Cells” focuses on thin amorphous carbon interlayers. The central question is whether these layers can stabilize the interface between the lithium-metal anode and the (solid) electrolyte, thereby contributing to more reliable and longer-lasting battery cells. To this end, the first step will involve developing thin amorphous carbon layers and depositing them onto copper current collectors using an innovative laser-arc PVD process. The coated materials will then be tested in battery cells and compared with reference cells. The aim is to determine which properties of the interlayers are crucial for achieving the most stable interface possible within the battery cell.
In addition to technical performance, the project also considers the environmental perspective and the potential for transferring the technology to larger cell formats. On the one hand, a life cycle assessment (LCA) will be used to examine relevant material and energy flows as well as the environmental impacts of the approach; on the other hand, a concept for scaling the technology to larger pouch cells will be developed simultaneously. In this way, the project combines material development and cell research with environmental assessment and initial considerations for future scaling. The goal is to comprehensively evaluate the potential of amorphous carbon interlayers for more reliable lithium-metal batteries and establish a foundation for further development toward larger cell formats.
In the long term, more powerful and longer-lasting lithium-metal batteries could help reduce the weight of battery systems while enabling high energy densities. This could benefit applications where weight, performance, and range play a key role – from electric vehicles to aerospace and stationary energy storage systems.

title: ITRI Partners with eJoule, Inc to Develop Long-Life NCM Batteries and Expand Applications in Drones, Electric Vehicles, and Energy Storage - Batteries News
content:
ITRI Partners with eJoule, Inc to Develop Long-Life NCM Batteries and Expand Applications in Drones, Electric Vehicles, and Energy Storage
FREMONT, Calif., and HSINCHU, Taiwan, Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — As performance requirements rise across drones, EVs, and energy storage systems, medium and high-nickel NCM batteries are seeing strong momentum in high-performance lithium-ion applications, driven by their high energy density and ability to enable greater range and lighter battery designs. Ongoing advances in cycle life, safety, and commercialization are helping broaden their adoption across demanding applications. The Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI) has partnered with eJoule Inc. to advance next-generation mid- and high-nickel NCM battery technologies. The collaboration leverages eJoule’s high-performance single-crystal nickel-manganese-cobalt (NCM) battery cathode materials and integrates capabilities across cathode materials, electrode manufacturing, and cell engineering to accelerate the transition of advanced battery materials from R&D to production. The initiative targets applications including drones, autonomous robots, EVs, and energy storage systems, highlighting the R&D strength and commercial potential of Taiwan’s advanced battery materials ecosystem while supporting a more resilient, high-performance battery supply chain.
Jeffrey Kuo-Chan Chiou, ITRI’s Vice President and General Director of Material and Chemical Research Laboratories, stated that ITRI has long been dedicated to the R&D of battery materials and cell technologies. This collaboration with eJoule Inc. combines the R&D strengths of both organizations in materials and battery technology. eJoule contributes its high-performance single-crystal NCM cathode materials, while ITRI tailors cell specifications and capacity, optimizing rate capability, cycle life, and other electrochemical performance, creating a direct link between material properties and real-life cell performance. Testing to date shows that eJoule’s single-crystal NCM cathode materials offer advantages in cycling stability and capacity retention, maintaining stable performance even after extended charge-discharge cycling, with cycle life approaching that of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries. These results highlight the development potential of single-crystal NCM materials to balance high energy density with long service life while offering improved safety compared with conventional NCM materials, broadening the options for high-performance applications such as drones and EVs.
eJoule Inc. is a California based deep-tech battery materials company with established operations in both the United States and Taiwan. At the core of its technology is the proprietary Dynamic Crystallization® Process (DCP®), which produces single-crystal cathode active materials directly from solution droplets without the conventional precursor (pCAM) stage. The process simplifies manufacturing and eliminates waste associated with precursor processing, while enabling precise control over chemical composition, dopant distribution and particle crystallinity to support improvements in battery performance, stability, and safety. Built on the DCP® platform, eJoule has developed a portfolio of mid- and high-nickel NCM products for high-performance battery applications
Dr. Minduan Liu,
Vice President of eJoule Inc, said:
This collaboration brings together eJoule’s cathode material capabilities with ITRI’s expertise in electrode fabrication, cell development, and battery integration,
“Together, we can integrate development from powder through electrode to cell, accelerating the path toward commercially viable, high-performance batteries.”
ITRI is committed to deepening its partnership with eJoule Inc. to accelerate the advancement and commercial adoption of mid- and high-nickel cathode materials and battery technologies. content:
Agilent and University of Chicago Launch Center of Excellence for Energy Materials Research
Agilent CoE supports research on next-generation energy storage materials
SANTA CLARA, Calif. & CHICAGO–(
BUSINESS WIRE
)–Agilent Technologies Inc. (NYSE: A), a global leader in analytical and clinical laboratory technologies, and the University of Chicago, one of the world’s leading research universities, today announced a scientific collaboration to establish the
Agilent Center of Excellence (CoE) for Energy Materials Research
The Agilent CoE will be based at the University of Chicago Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering (UChicago PME) and will support the Energy Technologies Initiative (ETI), a partnership between UChicago PME and the University of Chicago’s Institute for Climate and Sustainable Growth focused on driving innovation in energy storage technologies through academic and industry collaboration.
Mike Zhang,
senior vice president and president of Agilent’s Applied Markets Group, said,
Advancing energy storage research requires both scientific expertise and the analytical capabilities to understand how complex materials behave and change over time,
“By combining the University of Chicago’s interdisciplinary research strengths with Agilent’s advanced instrumentation and applications expertise, this Center will give researchers greater capabilities to investigate these materials, tackle some of the toughest challenges in battery and materials science, and accelerate progress toward new solutions.”
The CoE will use Agilent instrumentation, including mass spectrometry and atomic spectroscopy, to help researchers investigate the materials and systems behind next-generation batteries, including batteries for electric vehicles and connected devices as well as grid-scale energy storage.
Stuart Rowan,
interim dean of UChicago PME and faculty director for ETI, said,
The most important questions in energy storage require expertise and tools from across disciplines.
”This partnership will expand the analytical capabilities available to battery researchers across the University and create new opportunities for faculty, students and trainees to work together. I’m excited that Agilent is helping strengthen the research environment needed to pursue this work across the University of Chicago and beyond,”
The CoE will support the work of the Energy Technologies Initiative by bringing together researchers from across the University of Chicago and other academic and industry partners. By combining this interdisciplinary expertise with Agilent instrumentation, the CoE will support the development of analytical methods and workflows for research on energy storage materials and systems.
Advances in energy storage will be important to applications ranging from electric transportation and connected devices to grid-scale energy systems. By expanding access to advanced analytical instrumentation and supporting application development, the CoE will help researchers investigate the materials and systems underlying these technologies.
Y. Shirley Meng,
Liew Family Professor at UChicago PME and co-director of the Energy Transition Network, said,
Advancing battery research takes more than developing a promising material; we need to understand how materials perform, interact and change throughout a battery’s life,
Meng’s research combines first-principles, computation-guided materials discovery with advanced characterization using electron, neutron and photon sources. “The Center will give researchers across the University access to some of the most advanced analysis tools for deciphering the degradations in energy storage and conversion materials and devices.”
Battery development increasingly depends on precise answers about composition, impurities, interfaces and degradation pathways, all of which can influence battery performance, lifetime, and safety. The CoE will bring advanced analytical capabilities into the research environment where those questions are being investigated.
Shrayesh Patel,
associate professor at UChicago PME, a deputy director of ETI and director of the Center for Organic Battery Innovation (COBI), said:
The batteries we rely on today depend heavily on materials that can be costly, based on critical minerals, and challenging to recycle,
“At COBI, we’re exploring whether organic materials can offer a different path—one that could make energy storage safer, more affordable, and more sustainable by leveraging earth-abundant elements. Expanding the range of materials we can use in batteries is an important part of building a more sustainable energy future.”

Enevate Technologies Unveils Trifecta: Battery Technology That Ends the Energy, Power, and Cycle-Life Tradeoff
Longer drone flights, full-shift humanoid robots, lighter and faster race cars, and data centers that don’t burden the grid.
IRVINE, Calif., Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Engineers building drones, humanoid robots, race cars, data center power systems, and electric aircraft want more energy in less weight and space, plus the power to use it. Enevate Technologies today introduced Trifecta, a licensable cell technology designed so they no longer have to choose between energy density, power, and cycle life.
Battery engineers live by an unwritten rule: energy, power, or cycle life, pick two. At the cutting edge, they often get just one, paying for it with oversized packs, shorter missions, and lost payload.
Trifecta designs match or exceed the energy density of leading lithium-metal and solid-state cells without their usual safety and charge-rate problems, and long-life configurations reach 1,000 cycles.
Benjamin Park
, CEO of Enevate Technologies, said:
Engineers have spent years designing around their batteries
“Trifecta flips that. We want to have open conversations about how our technology can change how you design things.”
Trifecta comes in five modeled configurations:
Figures are for modeled designs that build on a successful proof of concept with earlier prototype cells.
Enevate Technologies works with each customer to match or tailor a configuration, then helps get cells built by a licensee, through a custom build, or by the customer’s existing supplier.
Battery manufacturers interested in licensing Trifecta to produce cells for their own customers are invited to reach out.

title: GWM’s Svolt began mass production of 100 kWh semi-solid batteries - Batteries News
content:
GWM’s Svolt began mass production of 100 kWh semi-solid batteries
GWM’s Svolt began mass production of 100 kWh semi-solid batteries, also called liquid-solid in China. Such a pack is built on the 900V high-voltage system, supporting 6C charging. This battery is capable of adding 500 km of range in 12 minutes of charging.
Svolt was formed by GWM back in 2012 as a subsidiary focused on EV battery production. It became independent in 2018. However, Svolt is still tightly connected to GWM, remaining its core supplier and strategic partner. On October 26, the company’s officials revealed that the first “Dragon Armor” hybrid semi-solid battery rolled off the production line in Changzhou. According to Svolt representatives, semi-solid packs with ternary chemistries are a “long-term technological path.”
There is currently no information about which vehicles will adopt the newly released battery. CarNewsChina expects the Wey V8X BEV to get this pack among the first vehicles. However, Svolt chairman and CEO Yang Hongxin said that more information about this battery will be revealed soon. He also added that this pack adopts a cell-level separator transfer-printing technology. It reportedly improves battery safety during fast charging. Thanks to the liquid cooling tech, this battery supports 6C charging, allowing it to add 500 km of range in 12 minutes.
A theoretical lifetime of this battery is over 1 million km, as it can achieve 3,000 charging cycles. At the same time, it adopts six layers of protection, reportedly offering impact protection three times the level of the Chinese governmental standard.
Svolt first revealed plans to mass-produce its semi-solid batteries in May 2026. However, it initially aimed to roll out the first batch in September. At the same time, Svolt officials highlighted that pure solid-state batteries are still distant from mass production. According to China EV DataTracker, Svolt’s battery installations from January to September 2026 reached 11.27 GWh (4.23 GWh LFP and 6.99 GWh ternary NMC). It currently holds 2% of the market share in China. The company aims to achieve a full-scale transition to hybrid solid-liquid technology for its ternary battery cells by the end of 2027, and plans to launch its third-generation hybrid solid-liquid technology in 2028

Gumi City Launches Battery Demonstration Center to Expand Advanced Industries
Following semiconductor and robot complexes, Gumi strengthens secondary battery sector with new infrastructure
A demonstration center for comprehensively managing batteries, secondary batteries, will be established in Gumi, North Gyeongsang Province.
On October 28, the groundbreaking ceremony for the BaaS, Battery as a Service, test demonstration center was held at the First Industrial Complex of the Gumi National Industrial Complex, hosted by the Korea Testing & Research Institute (KTR). Approximately 300 attendees, including Gumi Mayor Kim Jang-ho, Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan, Gyeongbuk Vice Governor for Economy Yang Geum-hee, and KTR President Lee Seung-ryeol, participated.
BaaS is a business model that provides various services related to batteries, including repair, rental, charging, and reuse. The BaaS test demonstration center, built on a 24,576-square-meter site within the First Industrial Complex, spans a total floor area of 4,231 square meters and consists of six buildings. The total project cost amounted to 27.2 billion Korean won.
The center evaluates the performance and safety of used batteries and supports their reuse in energy storage systems, ESS. KTR plans to provide full-cycle services for secondary batteries—from manufacturing to reuse—by integrating the center with its existing testing and certification systems.

content:
Basquevolt and Battera Technologies announce strategic collaboration to develop next-generation integrated battery solutions for high-performance aerospace applications
Vitoria-Gasteiz / Irún, October 2026.
Basquevolt S.A., Europe’s leading developer of lithium metal solid-state battery technology and manufacturer of high-energy-density battery cells, and Battera Technologies S.L., a specialist in the development, manufacturing and industrialisation of advanced battery systems, today announced a strategic roadmap to jointly develop and deliver integrated battery solutions targeting aerospace applications requiring the highest levels of energy density, safety, reliability and European sourcing.
A shared ambition: European-made batteries for high-performance applications worldwide
The partnership brings together two complementary technology capabilities: Basquevolt’s design and manufacturing of next-generation electrolyte and lithium metal cells, which already deliver energy densities exceeding 400 Wh/kg, well beyond today’s commercial lithium-ion cells, and Battera’s battery system development, manufacturing and industrialisation capabilities, including experience in demanding aerospace programmes.
Building on this performance, both companies are targeting a clear roadmap to exceed 500 Wh/kg in the coming months, a performance threshold that positions their joint solution significantly ahead of any commercially available advanced battery systems globally.
Pablo Fernández Santos,
Managing Director of Basquevolt, said:
This collaboration marks a pivotal step in Basquevolt’s strategy to deploy our technology in the highest-value applications where energy density is not a convenience but a critical requirement,
“Battera brings its expertise in battery pack development, manufacturing and integration, enabling high-energy-density solutions with rapid industrialisation and scalable production. Together, we are building something that does not yet exist at scale in Europe.”
Javier Llamazares,
Managing Director of Battera Technologies, said:
At Battera, we believe that developing advanced battery solutions requires close collaboration between cell development and battery manufacturing from the start,
“Through this partnership, Basquevolt’s advanced lithium metal technology and cell manufacturing capabilities, together with Battera’s experience in battery pack development and manufacturing, will allow us to deliver batteries with high energy density, tailored to the needs of aerial platforms, with production capabilities and scalability not currently available in Europe.”
Industrial production targeted for 2027, with the highest European content
Beyond research and development, the partnership is oriented from the outset toward industrial-scale production. Both companies have agreed on a phased industrialisation roadmap, with series production of integrated battery solutions targeted for 2027. The full value chain, from electrolyte and cell manufacturing to pack integration and system delivery, will be anchored in Europe, delivering what both companies believe will be the highest European content of any comparable high-performance battery solution available in the market.
The partnership reflects a deliberate commitment to European technological sovereignty in advanced battery technology, at a moment when access to high-performance, domestically produced battery solutions is increasingly recognised as a strategic priority across the continent.

content:
EnerSys To Acquire Ultralife, Expanding Differentiated Battery Technologies and Accelerating Growth in Defense Market
Accelerates EnerSys’ growth in mission-critical defense applications particularly high growth drone and counter drone systems
Expands advanced, differentiated battery technologies with U.S.-based manufacturing
Increases manufacturing capacity for specialized FEOC-compliant batteries
Supports multiple avenues for value creation, including extending EnerSys’ capabilities into new applications within core markets, accelerating growth in existing high-growth areas, and realizing significant cost synergies
READING, Pa.–(
BUSINESS WIRE
(NYSE: ENS), a global leader in stored energy solutions for industrial, infrastructure, and defense applications, today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Ultralife (NASDAQ:ULBI) for $16.00 per share in cash, representing a 166% premium to Ultralife’s unaffected closing share price on October 26, 2026. The transaction represents an enterprise value of approximately $320 million. EnerSys expects to realize $15 million to $20 million in annual run-rate cost synergies within the first 18 months, reflecting the unique benefits of combining Ultralife with EnerSys.
Ultralife is a leading provider of rechargeable and non-rechargeable batteries, battery systems, and related accessories for military communications and other specialized applications. The company serves government, defense, and commercial customers globally and generated $191 million in revenue in fiscal 2025. Headquartered in Newark, New York, Ultralife employs more than 700 people, with principal operations across the U.S., Canada, U.K., and China.
“This acquisition is a compelling strategic fit for EnerSys and directly advances our strategy to build a broader, more differentiated defense power platform,” said Shawn O’Connell, President and Chief Executive Officer of EnerSys. “Building on the success of our recent acquisitions, Ultralife expands our portfolio of advanced, reliable, high-performance power solutions. Together, we will be better positioned to support the U.S. Department of War (DoW) and allied forces with leading-edge, cost-effective technologies for the increasingly electrified battlefield of the future. We know the Ultralife business and its team well, and are confident that our shared commitment to engineering, problem solving, and customer focus will create a strong cultural fit. We look forward to combining our strengths to accelerate growth, enhance performance, and deliver greater value to our customers and shareholders.”
Mark Matthews, Chief Technology Officer and President, Precision Power Solutions, added, “Ultralife complements our multi-chemistry expertise and our liquid reserve technologies with an impressive patent portfolio and strong, longstanding customer relationships. Ultralife’s products offer exceptional capabilities such as very high energy density, long shelf life, low self-discharge, useful pulse power, and cold-weather performance, which are ideally suited to the growing defense mission profiles of today and tomorrow.”
Michael Manna,
President and Chief Executive Officer of Ultralife, said:
Combining with EnerSys is an exciting next step that will allow us to unlock value and growth opportunities for both companies, while delivering substantial and certain cash value to Ultralife shareholders,
“This transaction is a testament to the hard work and dedication of our entire organization, and now offers even greater opportunities for our valued employees. We look forward to partnering with the EnerSys team with the combined scale, resources, and shared vision to accelerate innovation and better serve our global customer base.”
Acquisition Expected to Offer Compelling Strategic and Financial Benefits
Expands EnerSys’ advanced defense power technology portfolio
with the addition of Ultralife’s differentiated multi-chemistry capabilities, purpose-built advanced manufacturing capacity with existing security and environmental permits, and operational expertise to scale production of EnerSys’ proprietary liquid reserve battery technology.
Increases scale and broadens exposure to the large and rapidly growing defense market
with capabilities across mission-critical applications in munitions, soldier power, drones, counter drones, and autonomous systems accelerating EnerSys’ focused growth strategy.
Deepens customer relationships
Supports an attractive financial profile.
The transaction is expected to be accretive to adjusted diluted earnings per share within approximately 18 months after closing, excluding transaction and integration costs and other non-recurring items.
Transaction Details and Timing
The transaction will be funded through cash on hand. The transaction has been unanimously approved by the Boards of Directors of both companies. Under the terms of the merger agreement, EnerSys, through a subsidiary, will commence a tender offer to acquire all of the outstanding shares of Ultralife common stock at a price of $16.00 per share in cash at closing, representing a total enterprise value of approximately $320 million. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including the tender of at least a majority of the outstanding shares of Ultralife’s common stock and receipt of applicable regulatory approvals, and is expected to close in the first quarter of calendar year 2027.
Advisors
XMS Capital Partners, LLC is serving as financial advisor to EnerSys, and Reed Smith LLP is serving as legal counsel to EnerSys in connection with the transaction.

title: Maxell and Institute of SCIENCE TOKYO Begin Joint Development of Next-Generation Batteries Based on 3D-SLISE Electrolyte Technology - Batteries News
content:
Maxell and Institute of SCIENCE TOKYO Begin Joint Development of Next-Generation Batteries Based on 3D-SLISE Electrolyte Technology
Targeting lower environmental impact and reduced fire risk through a manufacturing process free of flammable organic solvents
TOKYO–(BUSINESS WIRE)–
Maxell, Ltd.
(TOKYO: 6810) has launched a joint development project with researchers led by Specially Appointed Professor Yosuke Shiratori of the
Institute of SCIENCE TOKYO
(hereinafter “SCIENCE TOKYO”) on next-generation batteries utilizing an Aqueous Composite Quasi-Solid Electrolyte (
3D-SLISE
Because this next-generation battery does not use flammable organic electrolytes, it is expected to offer a reduced risk of fire. 3D-SLISE is an electrolyte containing water molecules at the interfaces between ceramic particles. By mixing it with water to form a slime-like electrolyte, batteries can be manufactured using coating-based processes.
This technology enables the use of coating technologies and production equipment that Maxell has cultivated through the manufacturing of lithium-ion battery electrodes. In addition, because neither dry rooms nor organic solvents are required, it is expected to contribute to reducing environmental impact through lower VOC (Volatile Organic Compound) emissions and reduced power consumption during manufacturing processes.
Furthermore, the battery is expected to offer excellent recyclability as 3D-SLISE can be dissolved in water after use, making it easier to recover active materials.
Potential applications include uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems for data centers, as well as power tools and automated guided vehicles (AGVs), where stringent safety requirements are essential. In particular, while lithium-ion battery-based UPS systems are increasingly being adopted in data centers to improve energy efficiency and reduce installation space, mitigating fire risks associated with thermal runaway and strengthening fire protection measures remain important challenges. Because even a single fire incident can significantly impact facility operations and business continuity, exceptionally high levels of fire safety are required.
Through this joint research project, Maxell and SCIENCE TOKYO aim to leverage 3D-SLISE, a water-containing aqueous composite quasi-solid electrolyte, to reduce fire risks and improve the safety of people and equipment. They also seek to contribute to reducing the burden associated with fire protection systems and lowering overall facility operating costs in data centers.

ADS-TEC Energy Advances One of Europe’s Largest Battery Storage Projects as Building Permit Nears
According to the permitting authority, all application documents are complete. The building permit is expected shortly. Planned to rank among the largest battery storage systems in Europe Expected to deliver grid stability, resilience and flexibility for Baden-Württemberg and beyond Developed with renowned European industrial partners and equipped with ADS-TEC Energy’s proprietary battery management technology Grid connection targeted for 2029 Multiple value streams for ADS-TEC Energy: proprietary technology, long-term technical services and a continuing stake in the project company Investor process well advanced; ADS-TEC Energy plans to sell a majority stake in the project company while remaining a long-term partner
NÜRTINGEN, Germany & MARKGRÖNINGEN, Germany–(
BUSINESS WIRE
)–ADS-TEC Energy PLC (NASDAQ: ADSE), a specialist in battery-based energy storage and fast-charging solutions, today announced that the permitting authority has confirmed that all application documents for its battery energy storage power plant at the Pulverdingen substation are complete. The building permit is expected shortly. With a planned power output of approximately 1 gigawatt (GW) and storage capacity of 4 gigawatt hours (GWh), the facility is intended to become one of the largest battery storage systems in Europe.
Power-plant scale
One gigawatt is roughly equivalent to the output of a large coal-fired or nuclear power plant, or of 250 wind turbines. The battery power plant is designed to deliver this output for approximately four hours, which corresponds to the daily electricity consumption of around 400,000 single-family homes or 800,000 apartments. Investment in a facility of this scale typically ranges from the high hundreds of millions to around EUR 1 billion.
Financial significance for ADS-TEC Energy
A flagship project for the region and for Germany as a business location
The project is a flagship from the region, for the region and far beyond. Large-scale battery storage systems are in the overriding public interest and support the implementation of the German federal government’s electricity storage strategy.
Thomas Speidel,
founder and CEO of ADS-TEC Energy, said:
A project of this size requires staying power.
”I am proud that we can build in Markgröningen, and above all of our team, which has spent years preparing this project. Energy is the foundation for everything we produce in Europe. Anyone who does not control the infrastructure for it gives up part of their ability to act. With our own technology and renowned European partners, we are demonstrating that Europe can plan, build and operate critical energy infrastructure on this scale on its own. We owe the fact that a storage power plant of this size and relevance can be built in Baden-Württemberg to the local landowners, the strong local community, the public authorities and the state government, as well as to our good cooperation with the grid operator,”
European partners and full technology control
Storage as the backbone of a renewable grid
Battery storage power plants do not generate electricity; they make it available when it is needed. The facility will absorb power when generation exceeds demand, for example at midday when solar output peaks or during periods of strong wind, and release it within fractions of a second when supply tightens. In day-to-day operation, it will typically run at partial load and adapt dynamically to grid requirements. It will also stabilize grid frequency, absorb load peaks and can support grid restoration after a power outage.
Today, surplus wind and solar power often has to be curtailed or exported at negative prices, only for supply to fall short a few hours later, when other power plants must step in. The storage system will shift this surplus into the hours when it is needed most. The result: less strain on the grid, fewer interventions by grid operators and a more robust and affordable power supply in Baden-Württemberg.
Rising demand for flexibility
Wind and solar generation is inherently variable, while electricity demand continues to grow, driven by electric vehicles, heat pumps and data centers, and fluctuates significantly throughout the day. Large-scale storage bridges this gap and makes a physical contribution to the stability of the power system. This role becomes ever more critical as the economy and everyday life increasingly depend on electricity.
Critical infrastructure built to last
The facility is designed to operate for decades. Beyond developing and building the plant, ADS-TEC Energy will provide technical services to ensure operational reliability and availability over the long term. The power plant is to be operated primarily together with partners from the European energy sector. Emerging flexibility markets will allow the plant to be marketed on the basis of its physical characteristics, and with full in-house capabilities across hardware and software, ADS-TEC Energy is well positioned to adapt the facility to evolving market conditions and new business models.
ADS-TEC Energy is currently in negotiations with potential investors and strategic partners. The building permit is a key prerequisite for concluding the financing and partnership agreements.
While a partner from the European energy sector is preferred, talks are also being held with renowned international infrastructure investors. ADS-TEC Energy intends to sell a majority stake in the project company while remaining a long-term project partner.

title: SK On Demonstrates ESS Fire Safety in Large-Scale Fire Test - Batteries News
content:
SK On Demonstrates ESS Fire Safety in Large-Scale Fire Test
SK On’s ESS meets UL criteria for large-scale fire testing
No thermal runaway observed in adjacent container during testing
SK On to accelerate global ESS market expansion following successful test
SEOUL, October 28, 2026
– SK On, a leading global battery manufacturer, announced that its energy storage system (ESS) met UL 9540A evaluation criteria in a large-scale fire test.
UL 9540A is a widely recognized North American test standard for evaluating fire and heat propagation during battery thermal runaway events.
The large-scale fire test (LSFT) simulates real-world ESS fire scenarios to assess the risk of fire spreading to adjacent containers. In March 2026, the testing requirements were strengthened to introduce more clearly defined criteria for evaluating fire propagation.
During the test, no thermal runaway was observed in the battery cells of the adjacent container. Temperature measurements inside the container also met the applicable evaluation criteria.
SK On attributed the results to its ESS design, which allows heat to dissipate gradually over an extended period. This helps prevent sharp increases in heat release rates and reduces the risk of fire spreading to neighboring containers.
SK On plans to accelerate its expansion in the global ESS market following the successful test.
In August, the company signed an agreement to supply lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries to U.S.-based ESS provider NeoVolta Power. In September 2025, SK On also signed a 1-gigawatt-hour (GWh) ESS supply agreement with U.S. renewable energy company Flatiron.
SK On is also expanding its presence in the South Korean ESS market. In February, the company secured 284 megawatts (MW) of ESS capacity, accounting for more than half of the 565 MW awarded in South Korea’s second round of competitive bidding for ESS projects.
The company is currently converting 3 GWh of its existing 7 GWh production capacity at its Seosan plant in South Korea into dedicated LFP battery production lines for ESS applications.
An SK On spokesperson
This test confirmed the fire safety of SK On’s ESS, demonstrating its ability to limit fire propagation and maintain key safety performance under simulated fire conditions,
“We will continue to enhance our safety technologies and product competitiveness to provide customized ESS solutions and expand our presence in the global market.”

title: EVIO Introduces the Deployable Battery Box, Part of Its Portable Power Family, Delivering Canadian-Made Aerospace Battery Technology for Rugged, Remote Defence Power Needs - Batteries News

EVIO Introduces the Deployable Battery Box, Part of Its Portable Power Family, Delivering Canadian-Made Aerospace Battery Technology for Rugged, Remote Defence Power Needs
OTTAWA, Ontario–(BUSINESS WIRE)–This week at the Aerospace Industries Association of Canada’s (AIAC) Aerospace Summit, EVIO unveiled the Battery Box, part of its Portable Power family—a Canadian-designed, modular battery energy storage system advancing toward prototyping for dual-use defence operations in remote, demanding environments. Drawing on high-energy-density lithium-ion battery packs developed for the EVIO 810 aircraft, this revolutionary product is designed to support dual-use customers who need substantial electrical power in a compact, rugged and transportable system.
The EVIO Battery Box delivers reliable, ruggedized, deployable power for defence and security applications, from Arctic and tactical operations to naval, land and air platforms, disaster relief and remote mining. Its modular design supports extended silent operation, powering communications, sensitive sensors and essential equipment while reducing acoustic and thermal signatures, generator run-time and fuel requirements.
Designed around a 147E standard military pallet, each EVIO battery box has an unparalleled energy storage capability that is 3 to 5 times higher than any other option on the market. This configuration can accommodate four EVIO battery boxes on a 463L standard military pallet, substantially reducing logistics costs to bring power to remote points of use with unprecedented megawatt power capability.
Michael Derman
, Co-founder and CEO of EVIO, said:
Defence operators need dependable power that can move with them, support demanding missions and allow periods of operation without a generator running,
“The EVIO Battery Box applies the electrification expertise we are developing for the EVIO 810 hybrid-electric regional airliner program for operational defence needs. It demonstrates how investment in aerospace technology can create new dual-use capabilities for Canada across defence and other industries.”
EVIO is developing a prototype, ready for testing in the first half of 2027. The prototyping activity includes multi-physics pack engineering, cell characterization, and physical multi-cell thermal runaway testing. A fully operational product will be ready for deployment in the first quarter of 2028. Development priorities include thermal management and performance in extreme cold to address the requirements of Arctic operations.
The EVIO Battery Box is being developed in parallel with the EVIO 810, sharing core energy storage technology and highest safety standards with the aircraft. The energy storage system enables zero-emission all-electric operation for short-haul flights (under 100 nautical miles) and around airports, while using turbine engines for extended range or in-flight battery charging. With operations in Montréal, EVIO is leveraging Canada’s aerospace engineering expertise and supplier network, supported by strategic partnerships with established leaders across the aerospace, battery technology, and advanced materials sectors.

H2scan Unveils Integrated Battery Safety Platform to Help Protect Critical Infrastructure From Emerging Battery Risks
HY-GUARD is the only platform to deliver early hydrogen detection and centralized safety visibility across lead-acid, nickel-cadmium and lithium-ion battery systems.
VALENCIA, Calif.–(
BUSINESS WIRE
)–As critical infrastructure operators face growing pressure to maintain uninterrupted power while managing increasingly complex battery installations, H2scan® today unveiled its HY-GUARD® battery safety monitoring platform, the only system of its kind that brings together self-calibration, continuous hydrogen detection, early warning capabilities and centralized system visibility to help operators identify developing battery hazards before they escalate.
The platform builds on H2scan’s recently introduced HY-GUARD RS and HY-SIGHT technologies, which extended the company’s hydrogen monitoring capabilities into lithium-ion battery applications. Together with HY-GUARD monitoring products, the integrated system supports monitoring across lead-acid, nickel-cadmium and lithium-ion batteries, and provides a flexible path from localized detection to system-wide battery safety visibility.
Designed for applications ranging from individual battery cabinets to large-scale energy storage facilities, HY-GUARD helps operators move beyond isolated alarms toward a more comprehensive understanding of battery safety conditions. Its continuous monitoring capabilities provide early indications of developing problems, giving facility and safety teams the necessary time to investigate, respond and prevent an abnormal, or potentially dangerous condition from escalating.
The cost of critical infrastructure failures is significant. According to Uptime Institute’s 2026 Annual Outage Analysis, 57% of surveyed data center operators reported major outage costs exceeding $100,000, with one in five exceeding $1 million.
David Ellis,
President & CEO, said :
For critical infrastructure operators, battery safety is no longer just about protecting equipment. It’s about protecting business continuity, equipment and personnel,
“As battery systems become more complex and the consequences of downtime grow, operators need to identify potential problems before they become costly failures. With HY-GUARD, we’re bringing together continuous monitoring, early detection and real-time intelligence to help facilities stay ahead of emerging risks and keep critical operations running.”
The HY-GUARD platform supports H2scan’s broader mission of turning self-calibrated continuous hydrogen data into actionable situational intelligence in order to help customers identify abnormalities sooner, reduce operational risk and protect critical infrastructure.

title: Inventus Power Launches the LV-24V50, a Compact 24V Lithium-ion Battery for Next-Generation Robotics and Material Handling - Batteries News
content:
Inventus Power Launches the LV-24V50, a Compact 24V Lithium-ion Battery for Next-Generation Robotics and Material Handling
The newest PROformance Li-ion Series battery delivers 1.2 kWh in a footprint sized for AMR and AGV chassis.
WOODRIDGE, Ill., Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Inventus Power (inventuspower.com), a global leader in advanced battery and power systems, today announced the launch of its LV-24V50, the newest addition to its PROformance Li-ion Series. Part of the PROTRXion® family, the LV-24V50 is a 24V lithium-iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) battery pack built for the growing power demands of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), automated guided vehicles (AGVs), and other material handling equipment. Samples are available now for OEM evaluation.
Compact, High-Power Design for AMRs and AGVs
Robotic and automated material handling platforms need more power density, faster charging, and smarter power management. The LV-24V50 delivers 1.2 kWh of rated energy and close to 5 kW of peak power in a compact package engineered for space-constrained robot and AGV chassis, so OEMs can integrate quickly and scale fleets without redesign.
Its 48Ah capacity is sized for full-shift runtime on small platforms without adding unnecessary cost, weight, or volume, which matters for OEMs running high-volume production programs.
The LV-24V50 can fully charge in approximately one hour, keeping fleets in service longer and reducing time spent on the charger in continuous warehouse, manufacturing, and logistics operations.
Intelligent Power Management with a Proprietary BMS
At the core of the LV-24V50 is Inventus Power’s proprietary battery management system (BMS). CANopen communication, soft-start pre-charge control, and active cell balancing work together to optimize performance, safety, and battery life, while giving OEM engineers visibility into state of charge, system health, and fault conditions.
Integrated LED status indicators show battery health at a glance, so technicians and operators can check status without additional diagnostic tools, simplifying service and reducing fleet downtime.
Lower Total Cost of Ownership Than Lead-Acid
Battery-powered industrial equipment needs longer runtime, a smaller footprint, and lower total cost of ownership without sacrificing safety or serviceability. The LV-24V50 is designed to deliver all three.
As a replacement for legacy sealed lead-acid (SLA) batteries, the LV-24V50 offers up to three times the cycle life and 40% less weight, helping OEM customers increase uptime and reduce fleet operating costs.
Torin Schneider,
Senior Product Manager, Inventus Power, said:
Robotics and material handling OEMs have been asking for a smarter, more compact 24V lithium battery, one that charges fast and reports its own health.
The LV-24V50 delivers exactly that. Designed for space-conscious AGV and AMR integration, it gives engineers the data they need from day one. We expect it to become a reference platform for 24V lithium in next-generation autonomous systems,”

title: Draslovka to Acquire ex-Natron Energy Battery IP, Completing a Vertically Integrated Western Sodium-Ion Value Chain - Batteries News
content:
Draslovka to Acquire ex-Natron Energy Battery IP, Completing a Vertically Integrated Western Sodium-Ion Value Chain
Acquisition gives Draslovka control of former Natron Energy IP portfolio spanning sodium-ion materials, cells and complete battery systems.
Deal combines acquired IP with Draslovka’s existing chemistry and European cathode-material capabilities, bringing key parts of the sodium-ion value chain together within one Western-aligned group and its partners.
The IP acquisition strengthens Draslovka’s position across the emerging Western sodium-ion battery value chain.
Technology targets applications where safety, high power, long cycle life and performance across a wide temperature range are critical, including data centers, grid storage, defense, industrial fleets, telecoms, rail and aviation.
The acquired IP will substantively boost Draslovka’s technology offering, a portfolio of transformative and protected innovations for specific industries.
MEMPHIS, Tenn. & PRAGUE–(
BUSINESS WIRE
)–Draslovka’s US-based subsidiary, COVORO MINING SOLUTIONS LLC (Covoro), the operator of one of the largest solid sodium cyanide plants in the world, today announced that it has agreed to acquire the intellectual property portfolio in Prussian Blue Analogue (PBA) and Prussian White Analogue (PWA) sodium-ion battery technology originally developed by Natron Energy.
Prussian Blue and Prussian White Analogues are not a single material but a tunable family of framework materials, and the portfolio protects that family across the whole stack — active-material synthesis, electrodes, electrolytes, cell design and manufacturing, as well as complete battery systems — through issued and pending patents, trademarks, and manufacturing know-how, with protection extending into the mid-2040s. The agreement covers intellectual property and intangible assets only and was subject to review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS), which granted clearance as a condition to closing.
The transaction consolidates PBA and PWA capabilities within a group of close West-aligned allies and partners:
Upstream chemistry
– Where Draslovka is the world’s leading producer of sodium cyanide and the ferrocyanide feedstocks at the heart of these materials; cathode active material production, with Europe’s first industrial-scale Prussian White Analogue line starting up at Kolín, Czech Republic in partnership with Altris of Uppsala, Sweden, in which the Group is a strategic shareholder;
Materials, cell and systems intellectual property
– To be held by Covoro in the United States;
Commercial partnerships
– Including Altris’s collaboration with Clarios on serial production of low-voltage sodium-ion systems that carry the technology into finished products. The complete supply chain is now built on Western-available inputs and Western-held intellectual property.
Pavel Brůžek,
CEO of Draslovk
The missing piece of the Western battery value chain has been the materials, and that piece now sits fully within Draslovka Group,
“Draslovka is now building an ecosystem to develop a Western sodium-ion supply chain based on both Prussian White and Prussian Blue technology, in the United States and in the European Union. We have already solved the production and scale-up of active material for both technologies at Kolín, and we now hold all the intellectual property rights associated with the technology, including the finished product and access to the US market. That means Draslovka can take this technology to market directly, and we will scale it with the partners who are ready to move at our pace.”
Jackson Briggs,
Strategy and Business Development Manager at Covoro
The strength of this sodium-ion technology is in applications where safety, power, cycle life and performance across a wide temperature range matter most,
“That includes data centers, grid storage and services, industrial fleets, telecoms, rail, aviation and other applications that need durable, fast-response batteries. We now have a technology platform that can be scaled with partners across those markets.”
Industry analysts now widely agree that sodium-ion complements rather than competes with lithium. While lithium optimizes for energy density, PBA and PWA batteries are intrinsically safe and not subject to thermal runaway, charge and discharge in seconds, and endure tens of thousands of cycles across a wide temperature range. Those characteristics satisfy fast-growing market demand from data centers and AI infrastructure as well as grid storage and services. They offer a durable alternative to lead-acid and nickel-cadmium batteries across automotive, telecom, rail, aviation and industrial standby. Taking account of the full life cycle, that durability makes them highly cost-efficient against competing battery technologies.
Within sodium-ion itself, the Prussian Blue and Prussian White Analogue family stands apart from the layered-oxide and polyanionic chemistries largely utilized by Asian manufacturers. PBA and PWA materials are made at low temperature from abundant sodium, iron and manganese through ferrocyanide chemistry the West already produces at industrial scale; they require no lithium, cobalt, nickel or graphite; they deliver class-leading power and cycle life; and they run on equipment compatible with existing lithium-ion lines. This is the one sodium-ion chemistry whose supply chain can stand entirely on Western ground today — a decisive consideration for data center, grid and defense buyers under tightening supply-chain and procurement rules.
With cathode-material production coming online in Europe, cell and system manufacturing is the remaining step to scale. Covoro and the Group intend to develop that capacity with selected partners — potentially through materials supply and licensing, cell technology licensing and co-located manufacturing. Draslovka will seek opportunities for demand-led scale-up both in Europe and the United States utilizing existing infrastructure.

content:
New US Department of Energy Consortium Advances SI-Driven Battery Manufacturing to Strengthen the Country’s Competitiveness
LEMONT, Ill.–(
BUSINESS WIRE
)–The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Argonne National Laboratory is joining DOE’s Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL), Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) and National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) in a
new national consortium
aimed at accelerating the transition of energy storage innovations from discovery to domestic manufacturing.
Called the Battery Manufacturing (BattMan) Accelerator, the consortium will tackle key challenges in scaling emerging battery technologies, with a focus on lowering manufacturing costs, shortening development timelines and strengthening U.S. leadership in advanced energy storage.
Jie Xiao,
Battelle Fellow at PNNL with a joint appointment as Boeing Martin professor of mechanical engineering at the University of Washington in Seattle, said :
Breakthroughs in battery science must be matched by our ability to manufacture them at scale. BattMan brings together the tools, data and partnerships needed to design manufacturable solutions from the start and accelerate their transition into industry,
The four laboratories contribute complementary strengths to bridge gaps between lab discovery and commercial production. PNNL will apply manufacturing science to show that new materials and processes can scale. Argonne will expand this work by validating feasibility and increasing production using its pilot lines. Both labs will provide materials — such as powders and electrodes — to ORNL for smart coating process development. NLR will lead the integration of advanced characterization, physics-guided quality control and digital materials design for rapid feedback to project partners.
Jianlin Li,
director of the Energy Storage and Conversion department at Argonne, who serves as the lab’s lead on the project, said :
Argonne brings materials synthesis and process scale-up capabilities that can shorten the time required for new technologies to reach commercialization,
​“Demonstrating technical and economic feasibility at larger production volumes is essential for validating new technologies efficiently.”
BattMan will also strengthen critical mineral supply chains by advancing battery materials made from more abundant domestic elements.
In addition to Argonne, PNNL, ORNL and NLR, the BattMan Accelerator includes the University of Washington, Binghamton University, University of Alabama, Arizona State University and University of Michigan-Dearborn as founding partners. The accelerator is actively establishing collaborations with companies across the battery and materials manufacturing sector. The laboratories will work closely with these university partners and industry to test and validate manufacturing processes at increasing scales and toward commercially viable production.
Claus Daniel,
associate laboratory director for Argonne’s Advanced Energy Technologies directorate, ​said :
To advance the next generation of battery technologies, we must reduce the risks associated with scaling innovations from laboratory discovery to commercial production,
Processes that work at small scale can behave very differently at larger volumes. Addressing those uncertainties earlier with better science, reliable data and rigorous validation gives companies greater confidence to invest.”
SI-driven manufacturing
Super intelligence (SI), also known as artificial intelligence, is expected to play a central role in the initiative.
SI-driven methods that use processing and manufacturing data have the potential to speed up discovery of new materials, improve efficiency of laboratory processes and support predictive, cost-effective design,
Beyond enabling high throughput, SI has the potential to optimize workflows to reduce cost and accelerate technology maturation,
​“The Argonne team will begin by applying SI to individual processes and later integrate SI models across full production line.”
As part of BattMan, Argonne will generate synthesis and scale-up data, train machine learning models and identify optimal processing conditions through active learning.
Scientific goals
In the near term, BattMan will deploy high-throughput experimentation, automated synthesis and characterization, and digital manufacturing tools to improve data quality, reproducibility and process consistency across partner institutions.
Longer term, the consortium aims to develop self-optimizing manufacturing systems using real-time data, digital twins and tight closed-loop control. BattMan will build on the autonomous laboratory concepts by advancing autonomous pilot lines designed to reduce scale-up time and costs, accelerate commercialization and reinforce domestic supply chains.
BattMan is currently forming industry partnerships in battery and battery-materials manufacturing. For institutions and companies interested in participating, visit
