LG Energy Solution Opens ‘Battery Innovation Contest (BIC) 2026’ to Connect Innovative Research Ideas with Industry Needs
The company invites universities and research institutions worldwide to submit innovative battery research proposals from Oct. 29 to Dec. 6
Thematic and Open-Topic calls for proposals are designed to deepen industry-academia collaboration, while a two-stage review process safeguards researchers’ original ideas
LG Energy Solution’s Battery Innovation Contest has supported approximately 50 research projects since 2017
SEOUL, South Korea, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — LG Energy Solution (KRX: 373220) today announced the launch of the Battery Innovation Contest 2026 (BIC 2026), a global open innovation program to discover and support cutting-edge battery technologies with strong commercialization potential.
Universities and research institutions in Korea and around the world are invited to submit concept proposals from October 29 through December 6, 2026, via LG Energy Solution’s online open innovation platform, BRIDGE (
). Priority will be given to proposals that address key pain points in the battery industry and have the potential to accelerate technological advancement.
Now in its 10th year, the BIC has enabled LG Energy Solution to pursue joint research with universities and research institutions worldwide. Through the program, the company seeks to help transform creative research ideas into commercially viable technologies while contributing to a stronger battery innovation ecosystem.
Deepening Two-Way Collaboration through Thematic and Open-Topic Calls for Proposals
BIC 2026 will continue to offer two calls for proposals designed to combine industry-driven research needs with the creativity and autonomy of researchers.
Under the Thematic call for proposals, LG Energy Solution presents specific research topics identified by its product development departments. This year, the company has significantly expanded the number of thematic topics, ranging from materials and cells to battery management systems (BMS) and AI. Researchers will be invited to propose solutions addressing these topics, creating a more structured framework for two-way collaboration.
The Open-Topic call for proposals will allow researchers to propose original ideas across broad areas of battery technology. This call preserves the researcher-led format, giving participants the flexibility to develop creative concepts with commercial potential.
Protecting Original Ideas through a Two-Stage Proposal Process and the BRIDGE Platform
To better protect researchers’ original ideas, LG Energy Solution will operate a two-stage application and evaluation process, in which applicants will submit a concise concept proposal during the first stage and a full proposal for further evaluation only after being shortlisted. Limiting the detail required in the initial review will help protect ideas that are not ultimately selected.
All proposals and subsequent research projects will be managed through BRIDGE, LG Energy Solution’s integrated, interactive platform for open innovation. BRIDGE streamlines industry-academia communication and project record management while protecting collaborative research technologies and minimizing offline administrative work.
A Decade of Impact: From Patent Filing to Publication in
Since 2017, approximately 50 research projects have been supported through the BIC. Topics with proven feasibility have been expanded into projects at the Frontier Research Laboratory (FRL), LG Energy Solution’s joint research center with leading universities and research institutions in Korea and abroad, which provides additional research funding as well as in-depth support from the company’s researchers.
The BIC has also delivered tangible results. For example, a patent application is underway for a physics-based model developed through a BIC project last year to improve BMS computation speed. In 2019, the FRL’s research on a long-life all-solid-state battery operating at room temperature was published in the prestigious journal
Je-Young Kim,
CTO of LG Energy Solution, said :
“Building on our differentiated technological competitiveness, LG Energy Solution will continue to accelerate its growth in the battery market.”

title: EV Battery Recycling Faces Supply Crunch
content:
Battery Recycling
EV Batteries
Automotive & Mobility
EVs last longer than expected, slowing the battery flow recyclers need to build a viable circular materials loop
November 5, 2026
8 Min Read
A Cox Automotive technician checks the health of a recovered EV battery pack.
Cox Automotive
At a Glance
Too few retired batteries exist to meet recycling demand yet
US lacks refining capacity after black mass export ban
GM closed loop proves recycled cells can power new EVs
There was a time when states applied a deposit to every glass soft drink bottle sold, adding a nickel or a dime to the price to encourage consumers to return the bottles for reuse rather than discarding them.
Because the mores of that era shrugged at littering, enterprising kids could set out for the neighborhood convenience store or gas station with no money, and by picking up a few discarded roadside bottles along the way, redeem them for their deposits and buy a piece of candy. Thus, was born a circular economy for
Coke bottles
employing child labor.
Why EV Battery Recycling Is Harder Than It Looks
The sought-after
circular economy for the materials in electric vehicles
, especially their batteries, is proving tougher to establish. This is in spite of the fact that today’s recovery processes are proving highly effective, even if it isn’t as simple as sanitizing glass Coke bottles for reuse was.
“Recycling processes can recover substantial quantities of critical battery materials—up to 95% for nickel, cobalt, and manganese and up to 80% for lithium,” reported Melissa Flaherty, Director of Sustainable EV Battery Ecosystem for General Motors in
a blog post
to the company’s media site.
Companies like Redwood Materials, founded by Tesla alum JB Strauble, promise to reprocess the depleted batteries from scrapped end-of-life EVs to recover the precious cobalt and nickel inside. Recently, the copper contained throughout EVs has also become more valuable.
Among Redwood’s partners in developing this circular infrastructure are BMW, General Motors, Toyota, Volkswagen of America, and Volvo from the auto industry, plus battery maker Panasonic and consumer goods seller Amazon. The company cites the more than six million EVs sold in the US over the last decade as a huge recycling opportunity, and claims that Redwood processes 70% of the EV battery packs that are recycled in the US.
The recovered elements at Redwood Materials, such as cobalt, lithium, and nickel. REDWOOD MATERIALS
Recyclers like Redwood and Cox Automotive dismantle cars, sending much of the vehicles’ materials into the conventional automotive recycling supply chain and targeting components like batteries, motors, wiring, and circuitry to recover valuable materials. Batteries are sorted to recover the ones that still have potential functional value in another role, such as stationary storage, and the rest are fed into industrial shredders, which break the materials down into a substance called black mass.
Black mass has nothing to do with Ozzy Osbourne’s music. Instead, it is a conglomeration of the valuable elements recovered from batteries, ready for processing back into those elements so they can be reused in new batteries. Battery material clearinghouse
Circunomics
describes this recovery of desirable materials “urban ore.”
Black mass recovered from EV batteries by Redwood Materials. RODNEY HANSEN FOR REDWOOD MATERIALS
Edgar Faler, Principal Mobility Analyst and Strategy for the
Center for Automotive Research
writes in the company’s October 2026 newsletter that “though still in its infancy, U.S. lithium-ion battery recycling already contributes an estimated $4.9 billion to GDP and supports nearly 24,000 jobs.”
Too Few Batteries, Too Little Refining Capacity
Which all sounds good. The problem is that those EVs that were sold are mostly lasting much better than was anticipated, reducing the expected inflow of batteries that are no longer suitable for powering passenger vehicles.
“The challenge with recycling right now is that there actually aren't nearly enough batteries to recycle as we would ultimately want, because we're still relatively early in the EV transition,” noted Sam Abuelsamid, vice president of market research at Telemetry, in
a YouTube interview with EV Pulse
“Probably 85% to 90% of all the EVs ever built have been built in the last five years, and those vehicles are still in service and probably will be for at least another five to 10 years, if not longer,” he said. “So the batteries in those vehicles are not ready to be recycled yet.”
A Cox Automotive technician lifts a defective battery module from its pack. COX AUTOMOTIVE
Redwood forecasts that approximately 1,000 gigawatt-hours (1 terawatt-hour) of EV battery packs will be recovered by 2040. However, the current slow emergence of this market suggests that this volume will be heavily back-loaded.
As a result, the EV recycling market is retrenching, reported Brian Skalovsky, Cox Automotive senior director of recycling. “The domestic shredding and capacity in the United States has gone down,” he observed. “We've seen two or three major startups that are in bankruptcy right now.”
There’s a bottleneck at the refining step of the recycling process in the US, he said. “There is virtually zero refining capacity in the United States right now. And I think that's a little bit of a problem right now, especially coming on the heels of the Bureau of Industry and Security’s (BIS) ban of black mass and tungsten export.”
That means that US recyclers can’t send their black mass abroad for processing unless the resulting materials are certified to be returned to the US for use in new products made here, Skalovsky explained. Without a way to refine the black mass in the US or the ability to send it abroad, recycling companies are being squeezed by the lack of a market for their product, putting a crimp in the circularity loop.
GM's Closed-Loop Experiment and the Second-Life Alternative
General Motors recently conducted a pilot closed-loop recycling project that saw the company employ materials recovered from retired EV batteries to build new batteries and install them into new cars. GM’s partner, Cirba Solutions, took 80 GM EV batteries and reduced them to black mass. This was used to create 12 tons of cathode active material for new battery cells that used 100% recycled nickel, cobalt, and manganese.
The company installed those cells into new Ultium battery packs and used those packs for new Cadillac Lyriq, Lyriq-V, Vistiq, Escalade IQ and IQL, Chevrolet Silverado EV Trail Boss, and GMC Sierra EV AT4 vehicles.
Batteries don’t have to be ground up to be reused. Those that are still in good shape are being routed into Redwood’s battery energy storage project, where slightly reduced capacity doesn’t matter. “We’re deploying roughly 10,000 GM second-life batteries into real-world energy infrastructure,” said GM’s Flaherty. “That includes the largest second-life battery microgrid in North America with additional deployments ahead, including at our own manufacturing footprint here in the US.”
“These batteries that come back through our door have a substantial amount of life left,” said Redwood Strauble. These packs retain 50% to 80% of their original capacity, he said.
“Today we are collecting, storing, moving, processing 20 gigawatt hours per year of batteries and battery materials, growing at over 100% a year,” Strauble said. “We have proven that we can quickly deploy these batteries back into a grid energy storage setting with a phenomenal value return. This architecture is flexible and fundamentally software-enabled, power electronics-enabled, to control and aggregate all these batteries together. No one's ever done that, even at a small scale, let alone at a large commercial scale.”
Redwood's battery energy storage system microgrid, with the packs located outdoors, where any fires can't spread. RODNEY HANSEN FOR REDWOOD MATERIAL
A potential complication in this market is the rise of cheaper lithium-iron phosphate batteries that could potentially be even cheaper than recycled batteries, said Skalovsky. “If I were an engineering company or a [battery energy storage system] builder, I would want a new module that has a 10-year warranty over something that's been in a vehicle that no one's going to guarantee,” he said. “I wouldn't feel comfortable designing something around used batteries. If there's a cheaper or equally priced new battery, I would go with the new battery.”
Motors, Magnets, and Rare Earth Recovery
Batteries aren’t the only component in an EV that contains valuable materials.
Market researchers Market Intelo
estimate the 2025 global market for recycled materials from EV motors was $3.2B. The company projects that will grow to $15.8B by 2034.
That is why Paladin recovers rare earth elements, copper, and other materials from retired EVs. “The [EV] rotor assembly is going to have those rare earth magnets in there,” said Luke Wray, Senior Vice President of Critical Materials & Defense at Paladin.
“But you're also going to have steel, you're going to have some copper, you're going to have some aluminum,” he said. “In some cases, you might have some circuit board that has precious metal value too,” he said. “So, when you add up all the pieces to the whole, and you're able to extract value at each level, that's where the economics start to make sense.”
“If I can shred the component when it comes into my facility, it makes sense to go after it,” Wray explained. Manual disassembly only pays off for very valuable materials. “If it has dysprosium in it, which we do see in the actual rotor assembly, for those magnets, we're seeing anywhere from 5% to sometimes as high as 10% dysprosium and trace amounts of terbium. Now it starts to get really interesting because those metals are going to fetch a much higher price.”
So, while EV recycling seems to have stumbled a bit out of the gate, continuing market pressure for the materials contained inside EVs that are on the road today ensures that there will be an industry to recover and reuse those materials. The only question is, “Which players will survive the current retrenching?” If only the solution were as simple as a 5-cent deposit to encourage reuse.

title: The Estée Lauder Companies & Microsoft Announce Partnership
content:
The Estée Lauder Companies & Microsoft Announce Partnership
Prioritise Us
on Google
Estée Lauder is partnering with Microsoft to bring more products to consumers. Credit: Estée Lauder
ELC is partnering with Microsoft to bring more personalised content to its customers, explains Brian Franz, Chief Technology and Transformation Officer
As part of its efforts to bring more innovation to its operations, The Estée Lauder Companies Inc. is partnering with Microsoft.
The partnership will involve the advancement of cloud and data foundation, alongside supporting responsible AI across the enterprise.
In doing this, ELC will be able to connect data better in order to develop more relevant consumer experiences and greater efficiency.
Network modernisation
In recent years, The Estée Lauder Companies has been integrating data and AI into its operations, working to
become more agile across the platform
and meet customer demand more efficiently.
Its One Operating Ecosystem strategy – a system, built over the last year – brings together data, shared platforms and strategic partners. The aim is to enable consistent, effective and scalable execution across functions and brands.
The partnership is a major part of this strategy, using the Microsoft platform to drive agility and AI across ELC. By doing this, the company’s data will be more connected, which results in more consistent access to data-driven insights. This reduces the risk of duplication and streamlines efficiency.
“As we continue to execute on Beauty Reimagined, we are building the future of consumer-centricity—in our products, experiences, commerce and more,” says Brian Franz, Chief Technology and Transformation Officer at The Estée Lauder Companies.
Brian Franz, Chief Technology and Transformation Officer at The Estée Lauder Companies
"Our partnership with Microsoft, in addition to the other strategic partners in our One Operating Ecosystem, is powering our teams with the capabilities to ultimately deliver more relevant, personalised experiences that meet consumers’ evolving needs.
“These enhanced capabilities will help us drive sustainable growth, improve productivity and support margin expansion, creating capacity to reinvest into our enterprise to serve our consumers.”
At a glance
ELC has four major product categories
Its products are sold in 150 countries and territories
ELC reached US$14.32bn in net sales for FY25
More than 20 brands sit under the The Estée Lauder Companies
Copilot tools have been expanded across more than 14,000 employees
A partnership for consistency
The partnership will result in a strengthened data foundation, which will make it much easier to run an AI-enabled consumer ecosystem. The strengthened data is crucial for expanding its
capabilities with AI tools
, as the company works to grow its understanding of consumer needs and preferences. Through this, the company can develop more personalisation within its products.
A large aim of the partnership is to be able to create more consistency in real time, across the discovery to purchase timeline, which then helps the brands understand the consumers and give them the ideal experience.
As a result, ELC is aiming to grow agility within its brands, helping them to adapt to new experiences and customer desires. Alongside this, this is a resilience driver for the company, helping it gain more flexibility as the way consumers shop continues to shift.
AI in supply chain
ELC is embedding AI in workflows and strengthening connectivity across functions, through its shared enterprise foundation. Through this, the insights become more accessible to team members, offering them a greater understanding of the business.
As a result, there is greater cohesion and connectivity across the supply chain. The insights are connected to end-to-end workflows, marketing teams, value chain leaders, commercial teams, as well as research and innovation teams. This results in faster and more coordinated decisions.
With consumer and market needs changing on a regular occurrence, fast response times are crucial. These greater insights result in a new type of process in getting products from launch to the consumer’s basket.
“The future of the beauty industry will be shaped by organisations like the Estée Lauder Companies that connect data, people and AI responsibly,” said Deb Cupp, EVP and Chief Revenue Officer at Microsoft.
Deb Cupp, EVP and Chief Revenue Officer at Microsoft
“Our expanded collaboration will help turn insights into action at scale—from empowering employees to modernising product development and delivering more meaningful consumer experiences.”
ELC is making secure AI tools, such as Microsoft Copilot, accessible to its employees. Through this, repetitive and manual tasks will be automated, meaning teams can put their efforts into strategy, innovation and higher-value decision-making.
More than 14,000 employees in the company have been making use of Copilot, embedding AI into their workflows and seeing improvements to their productivity. The partnership is part of ELC’s Beauty Reimagined strategy, which aims to increase consumer centricity and innovation within operations. Through the partnership, there will be increased growth
across efficiency, speed and agility
These enhanced capabilities will help us drive sustainable growth, improve productivity, and support margin expansion, creating capacity to reinvest into our enterprise to serve our consumers.

China blocks SoftBank’s US$5.37bn bid for ABB Robotics
Prioritise Us
on Google
ABB opened its robotics mega factory in Shanghai in December 2022. Credit ABB
Beijing has blocked SoftBank's US$5.37bn purchase of ABB's robotics division, the multinational has confirmed in a statement
China’s regulatory authorities have intervened to halt the acquisition of ABB Robotics, ABB’s China-based robotics arm, by Japanese technology conglomerate SoftBank.
SoftBank’s planned US$5.37bn acquisition of ABB Robotics has been prohibited by China’s National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC).
When the acquisition was
announced
in October 2025, the transaction had been expected to close in mid-to-late 2026, depending on regulatory approvals. Instead, it has been blocked by the NDRC, ABB confirmed on 5 November 2026.
“ABB confirms that it has been informed by SoftBank that the Office of the Working Mechanism for Foreign Investment Security Review in China has prohibited the acquisition of the ABB Robotics business in China,” an ABB statement announced.
The office operates within the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), as part of the wider Ministry of Commerce. The NDRC is closely involved in the development of China’s 5-Year Plans, although the responsibility for implementation of the plans is devolved to the relevant ministries; the office is also closely involved in efforts to develop and maintain competitiveness in strategically important sectors of the economy.
The latest intervention offers further confirmation of the sensitivity of cross-border acquisitions in the AI and technology space. The intervention by the Chinese authorities follows the NDRC’s blocking of a proposed takeover of AI start-up Manus by Meta in April 2026.
ABB Robotics has launched its first end-to-end, vision-based industrial-grade physical AI solution, integrating AI Robot Trainer into its Fashion Inductor module for automated fashion logistics. Credit: ABB Robotics
Cross‑border reach
ABB Robotics opened a US$150m robotics manufacturing hub in the Pudong district of Shanghai in China in 2022. The company makes 90% of its production for the Chinese market domestically.
alone accounted for 54% of industrial robot deployments in 2024, with its operational robot inventory surpassing 2m units. The country's market share has also climbed to 57%, representing growth from approximately 28% over the previous decade.
As ABB Robotics was originally founded in China, it remains subject to the country’s stringent export controls governing the transfer of domestic technology to foreign firms. While no rationale for the regulatory intervention has been announced, the potential integration of data from physical AI focused enterprises into AI models has been the subject of considerable interest.
When SoftBank originally announced its plans to acquire ABB's robotics division in October 2025, the deal was seen as a major element of the company’s
strategy
to invest in physical AI.
Neither the NDRC nor SoftBank have made any public comment about the intervention. ABB said in a brief statement that “ABB and SoftBank are in close dialogue and are working constructively on the transaction."
ABB Robotics has been supporting customers in all sectors of the Chinese economy from automotive and electronics to metals, plastics and logistics for decades. Credit: ABB
Meet the partners
CEO: Morten Wierod
Headquarters: Zurich, Switzerland
ABB is a global technology leader in electrification and automation, driving software-integrated engineering solutions to optimize manufacturing and robotics performance. ABB is the parent technology company behind the robotics portfolio. Its wider automation capabilities provide the corporate and engineering foundation for ABB Robotics’ physical-AI, robot-control and simulation platforms.
ABB Robotics
President: Marc Segura
Headquarters: Zurich, Switzerland
ABB Robotics provides innovative solutions for diverse industries including automotive, electronics, and logistics. Its services include AI Robot Trainer, which combines robotic motion, automatic path planning and lifecycle-based AI optimisation.
SoftBank
President: Masayoshi Son
Headquarters: Minato-Ku, Tokyo, Japan
SoftBank Group has invested in a number of physical AI start-ups across robots, tasks and environments, and maintains a strong focus on the integration of physical AI and AI models, including OpenAI.

title: AutoStore to Acquire Logiqs B.V. to Accelerate Automation
content:
AutoStore to Acquire Logiqs B.V. to Accelerate Automation
Prioritise Us
on Google
AutoStore has agreed to acquire Logiqs, in a move which will advance both parties' operations. Credit: AutoStore
Logiqs is expanding automation capabilities and meeting customer demand in developing acquisition journey, explains Reyer van der Louw, CEO of Logiqs
AutoStore has entered into an agreement to acquire Logiqs B.V., providing greater opportunity for growth.
The two companies will be collaborating to develop new technology and bring it to a wider market, which will be beneficial for both parties as the
supply chain becomes more automated
Accelerating advancements
Since 1975, Logiqs has been creating automation solutions for horticulture, vertical farming and warehouse logistics. Based in the Netherlands, the company designs software to
including iCUBE, an automated pallet storage system. The iCUBE has four-way shuttles and proprietary control software. Its technology is developed with the aim of making a better tomorrow, helping people do more with less resources and less waste.
Its warehouse technology is deployed at 30 customer sites, operating across a range of industries around the world.
“Today, we announced that AutoStore has entered into an agreement to acquire Logiqs B.V. This is an important milestone for our company and an exciting opportunity to further develop our iCUBE pallet storage technology together with AutoStore,” Reyer van der Louw, CEO of Logiqs said on LinkedIn.
Reyer van der Louw, CEO of Logiqs
“With over 50 years of experience in automation, we have built a strong foundation in engineering, software and product development. Combining our expertise with AutoStore's capabilities and international reach creates exciting opportunities to further develop our technology and bring automated pallet storage solutions to a broader market.
“I'm confident that the combined expertise of our companies, together with the cultural similarities we share, provides a strong starting point for a successful collaboration. I look forward to what we can achieve together.”
Logiqs is aiming to accelerate its technological capabilities with this new movement, gaining value from AutoStore’s
global reach and technological capabilities
. Despite this, it is maintaining its roots in horticulture.
Since its foundation, Logiqs has been collaborating with those in the horticulture industry to develop logistics solutions which support their daily operations. This relationship remains important to the company, and it will continue to support the industry amid its planned growth.
At a glance
AutoStore clients have seen storage capacity increase by 10x
AutoStore states customers have seen 50% in labour savings and 33% in cost savings over three years
AutoStore has approximately 2,000 systems across 68 countries
The iCUBE system consists of six compartments between -18C and +5C
40,000 pallets can be stored in an iCUBE system
Supply chain collaboration
International technology company, AutoStore, combines software, AI and automation to help with
storage and order fulfilment
. It has a compact storage system where robots travel above a grid in order to store and retrieve goods.
As part of the acquisition, AutoStore aims to expand its platform in order to include automated pallet storage, such as the iCUBE.

title: Kia's PV7 electric van stretches over 17 feet and seats 9
content:
Peter Johnson
| Nov 6 2026 - 7:30 am PT
is expanding its electric van lineup with the PV7, a larger PV5 sibling that can carry nine people or a whole lot of cargo.
The Kia PV7 van is launching in 2027
The PV5, Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business, is proving to be a bigger hit than expected.
A year after it went on sale, the PV5 quickly became Europe’s most popular small electric van. In the first half of 2026, it was the top seller in its segment, accounting for 37% of electric C-segment van sales across Europe.
Next year, Kia will launch the PV7, the second electric van from its PBV business. Kia
revealed the PV7
at IAA Transportation in Hanover, Germany, in September.
It’s based on the same E-GMP.S platform as the PV5, but the PV7 features a considerably longer wheelbase and stretched body, opening up more space inside.
The PV7 is over 17.5 ft long, measuring 5,350 mm long, 1,995 mm wide, and 1,990 mm high, with a 3,500 mm wheelbase. In comparison, the PV5 is just 4,695 mm long, 1,895 mm wide, and 1,915 mm tall, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.
That’s even bigger than the
Volkswagen ID. Buzz
Long-Wheelbase (LWB), which measures 4,962 mm in length with a 3,239 mm wheelbase.
Kia PV7 Passenger (Source: Kia)
23 different top hats coming
Like the PV5, the PV7 will initially be available in Passenger and Cargo body styles, but Kia plans to launch 23 different variants, or “top hats,” over the next few years.
It will be offered with two nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) battery packs: 71.5 kWh and 96.2 kWh. The Long Range Cargo model offers an all-electric WLTP range of over 460 km (285 miles). Even at full capacity, Kia said the new PV7 achieves nearly 400 km (248 miles) of range and still has 350 liters of trunk space.
A plena capacidad la nueva
consigue casi 400 km de autonomía y aún reserva 350 litros de maletero
#MovementThatInspires
Front-wheel drive (FWD) will be standard at launch, but Kia plans to add an all-wheel drive (AWD) option later.
Depending on the configuration, the FWD electric powertrain delivers up to 268 horsepower (200 kW) and 309 lb-ft (420 Nm) of torque.
Thanks to its 800V architecture, the Kia PV7’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in about 25 minutes with a 350 kW DC fast charger. It will be Kia’s first vehicle with two charging ports, including a front AC/DC port and an optional rear side AC port.
Kia PV7 Cargo (left) and Passenger (right) Source: Kia)
With vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, it can serve as a mobile power source for tools, equipment, a campsite, or other external electronic devices.
Personal and business use
The PV7 Cargo, designed for businesses, fleets, and logistics, is available in 2- and 3-seat configurations and offers up to 6.1 cubic meters of cargo space. The High Roof variant offers even more, with up to 8 cubic meters.
Maximum payload is up to 1,165 kg (2,568 lbs) for the Cargo Long and up to 1,200 kg (2,645 lbs) for the compact model.
The PV7 Cargo Long features a 550 mm loading height and, according to Kia, enough capacity for up to three Euro pallets (800 x 1,200 mm). An added heavy-duty mode adjusts the vehicle’s response to varying payloads to help maintain stability and control while driving.
Depending on the use, buyers can choose between full-open twin-swing tailgate doors or a lift-up tailgate.
The PV7 Passenger, on the other hand, is designed for personal use and families, or can also be used as a shuttle with room for up to nine passengers in the global version. In Korea, it will seat up to 11 passengers.
The 7-seater features Long-Rail Easy Remove Seats, enabling various interior seating configurations. The 9-seater variant, on the other hand, is available with or without a fourth row.
High-tech and spacious interior
Inside, both versions feature Hyundai’s new Pleos Connect infotainment system, with 12.9″ and 14.6″ display screens and physical controls for commonly used functions.
The system runs Android Automotive OS, making it more like a smartphone with apps and customizable screens. It also includes Hyundai’s Gleo AI, an AI-powered in-car companion that can answer questions, control navigation or vehicle functions, and more.
Kia said the PV7 is based on a “Mobile Workspace” concept, with a layered dashboard and center console to optimize space.
The Kia PV7 Passenger and Cargo will go on sale in Korea and Europe in the second half of 2027. It will then roll out to new markets with new derivatives and conversions.
Kia will announce PV7 prices closer to its launch. In Korea, the PV5 Passenger and Cargo Compact starts at 45.9 million won ($34,000) and 41 million won ($30,000), respectively. In Germany, the
PV5 Passenger
5-seater starts at €38,690 ($43,000).

title: Tesla hikes Cybertruck prices up to 10% after announcing it will kill production
content:
Tesla Cybertruck
Fred Lambert
| Nov 6 2026 - 6:03 am PT
Tesla has raised Cybertruck prices in the US by up to 10% and stopped taking orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim. The cheapest Cybertruck you can actually order now costs $92,490.
The move comes right after Tesla
confirmed it will end Cybertruck production
at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027.
The new Cybertruck prices
Here’s what Tesla’s online configurator shows today, compared to the prices set in August:
Dual Motor AWD: $82,490, up from $74,990 (+$7,500, 10%), but no longer orderable
Premium AWD: $92,490, up from $84,990 (+$7,500, 8.8%)
Cyberbeast: $102,490, up from $99,990 (+$2,500, 2.5%)
The Dual Motor trim still shows a new, higher price on Tesla’s website, but the option is greyed out. So Tesla raised the price of a version it isn’t selling anymore.
This is the second price hike in less than three months. Tesla
raised prices by $5,000 on two trims in August
, when the Dual Motor went from $69,990 to $74,990 and the Premium AWD from $79,990 to $84,990.
Add it up and the Premium AWD is now $12,500 (15.6%) more expensive than it was in early August. And the entry price for any Cybertruck you can order went from $69,990 to $92,490. That’s a 32% jump in about 10 weeks.
For reference, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in 2019 with a promised starting price of $39,900.
Higher prices on a truck nobody’s buying
The price hikes make little sense from a demand standpoint. Tesla doesn’t break out Cybertruck deliveries, but its “Other Models” category, which also includes the Model S, Model X, and Semi, fell 48% year-over-year to 8,295 units in Q3. We estimate Cybertrucks made up 7,000 to 8,000 of those, about 12% of the line’s 250,000-unit annual capacity.
Tesla also tried the opposite approach earlier this year. It offered a dual-motor Cybertruck at $59,990 in February for “only the next 10 days,” then pulled it. A single-motor RWD version was discontinued after just 173 sales. None of it moved the needle.
The Cybertruck isn’t sold in Europe or most right-hand-drive markets, and Tesla
canceled it for Australia and New Zealand
last month.
Electrek’s Take
This is what a wind-down looks like. Tesla isn’t trying to sell more Cybertrucks anymore. It’s trying to make as much money as possible on the last ones, with the hope that announcing the end of production will encourage some people to secure their order.
Once you’ve decided to end a program, volume stops mattering. You have a set number of build slots left, a parts supply you want to burn down, and probably a small group of fans who’ll want one before it’s gone. Pausing the cheapest trim and charging $7,500 more for the rest is the obvious play. You push everyone into higher-margin configurations and stop pretending the base truck is a real product.
But it does say a lot about the last two years of Cybertruck pricing. Tesla went from a $59,990 “limited-time” offer in February to a $92,490 entry price in November. That’s a company that never figured out who the truck was for.

title: Lucid teases its cheaper sub-$50,000 Cosmos EV in new video and images
content:
lucid cosmos
Fred Lambert
| Nov 6 2026 - 5:42 am PT
The rear of the vehicle in Lucid's new teaser video (Image: Lucid)
Lucid has released a new teaser video of what looks like the Cosmos, its upcoming sub-$50,000 midsize electric SUV and the car that’s supposed to turn Lucid into a volume automaker.
The clip gives us the clearest look yet at the Cosmos’ lighting, front and rear, after months of camouflaged prototype sightings. But the car itself is still about a year away.
Same design Lucid filed in Europe
Lucid posted the 1 minute 34 second video
yesterday. The caption talks about “elevating the experience of movement” and says Lucid can’t wait “to share this feeling with even more people.” It doesn’t name the vehicle, but “even more people” is about as subtle a hint at a cheaper model as you can get.
Two frames from the film show the vehicle at dusk. At the rear, “LUCID” is spelled out in red illuminated letters across the tailgate, flanked by thin red light strips, with a spoiler cutting across the base of the rear glass. Up front, a sculpted LED headlight with a row of vertical segments sweeps across a red body panel.
The rear of the vehicle in Lucid’s new teaser video (Image: Lucid)
That rear end matches the
Cosmos design Lucid registered with the EU Intellectual Property Office
in May, which showed the same spelled-out “LUCID” tailgate and rear-glass spoiler. It also lines up with the thin red light strips on the
camouflaged Cosmos prototype spotted on Highway 101 in California
last month.
A headlight detail from Lucid’s new teaser video (Image: Lucid)
Lucid Cosmos
unveiled its plans for Cosmos and Earth at its first Investor Day in March
. Both ride on the new midsize platform and start under $50,000, roughly half the price of the Gravity.
On paper, the Cosmos is impressive. Lucid claims about 300 miles of range from a 69 kWh pack, thanks to efficiency of up to 4.5 mi/kWh, which it says is 10% better than its closest competitor. It also claims 200 miles of range in 14 minutes of charging, and its new Atlas drive unit has 30% fewer parts and costs 37% less than the Zeus unit in the Gravity.
The problem is timing. Production was supposed to start in late 2026. In August, CEO Silvio Napoli
pushed the Cosmos to 2027
, “most likely the second half.”
That puts it on the same schedule as Rivian’s $45,000 base R2, and well after the Tesla Model Y it was
caught testing next to in Arizona
back in May.
Electrek’s Take
Lucid needs this car badly. It delivered 3,806 vehicles in Q3, down 7% year-over-year, while building only 2,954 after cutting the second shift at its Arizona factory.
The company is building hype a year out. It has nothing else new to sell until the Cosmos arrives, and the company reports Q3 earnings on Monday. They need to remind everyone what they are working toward.
A midsize SUV doing 4.5 mi/kWh would be best in class by a wide margin, and Lucid’s efficiency claims have held up on the Air. If it really lands under $50,000 with 300 miles of range, it’s a very compelling alternative to the Model Y and the R2, which still have room to take over market shares from ICE vehicles.
But Lucid has already slipped this car once; it says its cash lasts “well into 2027,” and the Cosmos is due in the second half of 2027. That’s a tight overlap. I think the Cosmos will be a good car, but can Lucid fund it all the way to customers’ driveways?

title: Liebherr expands excavator range with new, 250-tonne electric model
content:
Electric Heavy Machinery
Liebherr
Jo Borrás
| Nov 6 2026 - 4:49 am PT
It takes some seriously heavy equipment to make an ultra-class mining truck look little
, but that’s exactly what German equipment giant Liebherr does best, and its newest, 250-tonne production excavator keeps that tradition alive – only this time, it’s electric.
Liebherr began converting its diesel-powered mining excavators to electric in limited numbers back in 2024
, and electric power has proven to be effective –
moving millions of tons of dirt
saving millions of dollars in fuel and maintenance costs
. Now, the company is translating that testing experience into regular production practice with the launch of a new, all-electric machine. Meet the R 9300 G8-E.
Based on the proven R 9300 G8 platform, the new Liebherr R 9300 G8-E packs an 850 kW (~1,140 hp) electric drivetrain designed to IEC standards and supports 6-6.6 kV power supplies. The company says its electric setup offers customers the same hydraulic power and bucket capacity (1.8 tonnes/cubic meter, or ~1.5 short tons/cubic yard) as the diesel version.
All that electric power ships with advanced electronics and operator assistance systems designed to maximize both efficiency and safety while giving mine operators more data to work and plan with. Liebherr describes its take on ADAS thusly:
The R 9300 G8-E comes with Liebherr Power Efficiency – Hydraulic Control as standard, which adapts hydraulic power to suit the machine’s load profile, reducing overall engine load factor. Thanks to its Generation 8 electronic architecture, the R 9300 G8-E is compatible with a range of Liebherr’s IoMine technology products, including its range of excavator Assistance Systems, the semi-autonomous Bucket Filling Assistant, the Skyview vision system as well as the data visualisation tool, Data View. Customers also have the option of installing Liebherr’s autonomous cable reel solution onto the excavator to assist with cable management and support machine mobility on site.
LIEBHERR
Like its repowered cousins
, the big electric excavator does seem to have on-board batteries, but is primarily driven and operated with grid power,
reducing charging and re-charging concerns and enabling round-the-clock operations for as long as grid power holds
More efficient, more effective
Good-looking machine; via Liebherr.
Liebherr touts the benefits of new R 9300 G8-E’s quiet, emissions-free running throughout its official announcement, but doesn’t stop there. The company says its EV, which makes do with thousands of fewer moving parts in its drivetrain, can also reduce maintenance requirements and associated operating costs in certain applications and site conditions while improving workplace conditions for the people who work in and around the machine.
The electric drivetrain also reduces vibration inside the cab, improving operator comfort, limiting fatigue, and potentially contributing to a safer working environment.

title: Zoomlion says its new, 1,600 hp hybrid tractor is the world's most powerful
content:
Electric Heavy Machinery
Hybrid vehicle
Jo Borrás
| Nov 6 2026 - 3:48 am PT
Made with AI.
Chinese equipment brand Zoomlion showed up to this week’s China International Agricultural Machinery Exhibition with a new ultra-high-horsepower hybrid tractor that sets a new benchmark, offering more than 1,600 hp while cutting back on both fuel and fumes.
Zoomlion calls its new 9DX hybrid tractor a radical rethink of what a modern ag unit can be
, combining the all-day pulling power of a conventional diesel machine with the efficiency, accuracy,
and instant torque benefits of electric drive
. The company claims its hybrid setup can reducing fuel consumption, emissions, and deliver lower operating costs, without asking massive industrial farming operations to walk away from diesel entirely.
The tractor itself gets a headline-grabbing 1,600 hp Zoomlion 9DX features an 800V hybrid electric powertrain and continuously variable transmission that delivering a peak torque of 7,200 Nm (~5,300 lb-ft) of torque. Getting all that power to the ground is a four track tank-drive system riding on Zoomlion’s in-house developed 762 mm (~30 inch) wide tracks that are designed to distribute the tractor’s considerable weight for maximum traction and minimum soil compaction. What’s more, the high-traction treads can push the big machine to hit a maximum speed of 40 km/h across grades and slopes of up to 12 degrees.
The 9DX also gets a high-capacity hydraulic system capable of delivering 636 liters per minute of flow (~170 GPM), allowing it to work with some seriously heavy duty implements like ultra-wide seeders and variable-rate fertilizer applicators.
The Zoomlion 9DX was one of several new machines at this year’s exhibition, which hosted more than 3,000 exhibitors and vendors – but the big hp numbers all over the show made an even bigger impression, leading AGCO’s director of global electronic and electrical engineering, Nicolas Meunier, to tell Chinese State news agency Xinhua that
the country had moved on from producing mostly low-horsepower tractors
to building some seriously large machines.
There’s no official word on specs and batteries, but the company has developed an 800V modular battery pack system for its other equipment offerings that can scale from 140-800 kWh of capacity while other top-shelf Zoomlion tractors featuring an ag version of Cummins’ 15 liter turbodiesel.
The 9DX tops off what’s sure to be another record year for Zoomlion
, which is coming off strong early export quarters shipping into Germany, Australia, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

title: BYD's electric hypercar hits 312 mph, first production car over 500 km/h
content:
BYD YangWang
Yangwang U9
Fred Lambert
| Nov 6 2026 - 3:40 am PT
BYD’s Yangwang U9 Xtreme just reached 503.17 km/h (312.66 mph) on a closed highway in Abu Dhabi, making it the first production car ever to go faster than 500 km/h.
The FIA and Guinness World Records both recognized the run. It’s the all-electric hypercar’s second top-speed record in just over a year, and the one it broke was its own.
BYD announced the record on X this morning, saying the U9 Xtreme “has done the impossible” and calling it “the fastest production car on the planet.”
Abu Dhabi closed a 10 km section of the Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed International Road (E11), in the emirate’s Al Dhafra Region, for the attempt. That gave the team a 7 km straight. Marc Basseng, the German racing driver who set the car’s previous record, was behind the wheel again.
It took two days. Basseng maxed out at 490 km/h on the first day, per the FIA. After an overnight round of changes to the rear wing, damping, and tire pressures, he got to 503.17 km/h on his second attempt of November 1.
The previous mark was 496.22 km/h (308 mph), set at Germany’s ATP Papenburg proving ground in September 2025. That run had already pushed the Bugatti Chiron Super Sport 300+ and its 490.48 km/h from 2019 off the top of the list.
And it comes just days after BYD released footage of a U9 Xtreme
crashing into a guardrail at about 280 mph
during an earlier high-speed test. The driver walked away unharmed. BYD went right back out and hit 457.89 km/h on the next run.
3,000 PS, 1,200 volts, 30 cars
The U9 Xtreme is the track-focused version of the Yangwang U9, the flagship supercar from BYD’s luxury brand. It uses four electric motors, each rated at 555 kW and spinning up to 30,000 rpm, for 2,220 kW combined. That’s over 3,000 PS, or nearly 3,000 hp.
It runs on a 1,200-volt architecture with a track-grade version of BYD’s Blade Battery. Those are LFP cells, the same chemistry BYD puts in its cheapest city cars.
For context, the Rimac Nevera R, which
snagged a pile of EV world records last year
, tops out at 431.45 km/h. The U9 Xtreme also holds the production EV lap record at the Nürburgring Nordschleife at 6:59.157.
Only 30 will be built, and
BYD is charging around $3 million apiece
. Don’t expect to see one in the US, where BYD doesn’t sell passenger cars.
But there are asterisks
The biggest one: this is a single-direction run. The two Guinness titles listed for the attempt, highest speed by a production car and by an electric production car, are both specified as “single direction.” BYD’s post claims four Guinness records, but the FIA’s announcement only lists those two for this run.
Production car top speed records have traditionally been the average of two runs in opposite directions, within an hour, to cancel out wind and road grade. That’s how Koenigsegg got its 447.19 km/h record with the Agera RS in 2017.
Bugatti took heat for exactly this in 2019, when the Chiron hit 490 km/h one way on a pre-production car. Bugatti itself said it wasn’t an official record.
The car also ran on bespoke semi-slick tires developed with Giti Tire. It’s not clear whether the 30 customer cars will get them.
Electrek’s Take
Asterisks aside, this is wild.
A Chinese automaker best known for $10,000 city cars now builds the fastest production car in the world, and it’s electric. Not long ago, the conventional wisdom was that EVs couldn’t sustain high top speeds because the battery and motors would overheat long before the car ran out of road. BYD just ran 503 km/h on LFP cells. LFP cells!
But we’d hold BYD to the same standard we held Bugatti to. A one-way run on a highway with a 7 km straight is a great demo, not a definitive record, but impressive nonetheless.
And either way, let’s be honest: this is about marketing. Nobody is going to drive one of these 30 cars at 500 km/h. But it works. It’s a halo for Yangwang ahead of its new ultra-luxury sedan and for BYD’s push into Europe, and it makes the “Chinese cars are cheap copies” crowd look out of date.
Meanwhile, Tesla promised a Roadster that would hit over 250 mph back in 2017. Nine years later,
it’s still not in production
The real question now is whether Bugatti or Koenigsegg answers with a two-way 500 km/h run. Koenigsegg says its Jesko Absolut can theoretically do it, but it has never attempted a run. Is BYD what finally makes them try?

title: Tesla to end Cybertruck production as sales stall at ~10% of plan
content:
Tesla Cybertruck
Tesla Cybercab
Fred Lambert
| Nov 6 2026 - 3:33 am PT
Tesla is ending Cybertruck production. CEO Elon Musk announced early Friday that the automaker will “wind down” the electric pickup at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of 2027, about three and a half years after the first deliveries.
Musk says it’s to make room for more Cybercab production. But Giga Texas isn’t short on space. The Cybertruck is short on buyers, and it sells at roughly a tenth of the 250,000 units a year Tesla built its line for.
Here’s Musk’s full post on X:
Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production
That’s all he said. Nothing yet on how long Tesla will keep selling inventory or what happens to parts and service for existing owners.
Selling at a tenth of plan
Tesla doesn’t break out Cybertruck deliveries. It lumps them into “Other Models,” along with the Model S, Model X, and now the Semi.
That bucket tells the story anyway. Tesla delivered 8,295 “Other Models” in Q3 2026, down 48% year-over-year and the lowest since Q2 2021. With Model S and Model X production over since April,
we estimated that 7,000 to 8,000 of those were Cybertrucks
That’s a pace of about 30,000 trucks a year. Tesla planned the Cybertruck line for 250,000 units annually, and its latest shareholder letter still lists more than 125,000 units of installed capacity. So the truck is selling at about 12% of plan, and roughly a quarter of what’s actually installed.
The US numbers from Cox Automotive are worse. Cox estimates 3,519 Cybertruck sales in Q1 2026 and 3,744 in Q2, down from 14,416 in Q3 2024.
And not all of those were real customers. S&P Global Mobility data showed
SpaceX bought 1,279 Cybertrucks in Q4 2025
, and Musk’s companies took 1,339 in total, about 19% of US registrations that quarter. If it wasn’t for Musk’s self-dealing, the Cybertruck would probably be dead already.
Tesla tried to fix demand. It launched a cheaper rear-wheel-drive version in 2025 and pulled it months later, then brought a cheaper dual-motor trim to customers this summer. And then it raised prices by $5,000 in August. The dual-motor now starts at $74,990.
None of it moved the needle.
Giga Texas has plenty of room
The “make room” explanation doesn’t hold up. Giga Texas has more than 10 million square feet of factory floor, by Tesla’s own count, and the Cybertruck line is already running at about a quarter of its installed capacity. Most of it is sitting idle.
The Cybercab also isn’t at a volume where it’s fighting anyone for floor space. Texas had 463 Cybercabs registered as of late October, and Tesla built a separate line for its “unboxed” manufacturing process.
If Tesla needs more Cybercab capacity down the road, it has the space. What it doesn’t want is to keep paying for a truck with its own stainless steel body, its own castings, and its own supply chain at 30,000 units a year.
Electrek’s Take
Let’s call this what it is. Tesla isn’t ending the Cybertruck because the Cybercab needs room. It’s ending it because nobody’s buying it at anything close to the volume Tesla planned, and supporting a low-volume vehicle this unique is expensive.
I wouldn’t be surprised if Tesla lost a couple of billions on the Cybertruck experiment. Between R&D, pushing suppliers to produce 250,000 trucks per year, and deploying its own production line capable of 125,000 trucks per year, Tesla has invested billions. And with only ~70,000 trucks delivered in roughly 3 years, it probably never made any positive cash flow from the program.
The Cybercab line gives Musk a forward-looking reason to wrap a product failure in. Tesla did the same thing when it ended Model S and Model X production this year to free up Fremont for Optimus. It’s a lot easier to say “we need room for the future” than “this didn’t sell.”
We’ve said it many times: the Cybertruck is genuinely impressive to drive. Steer-by-wire and rear-wheel steering are real engineering, and nobody else has put them in a production pickup. But Tesla built a 250,000-unit factory for a polarizing $75,000+ truck that can’t be sold in Europe or most right-hand-drive markets. It
just cancelled it for Australia and New Zealand
two weeks ago. The math was never going to work.
It’s truly a sign of Tesla today. Musk used to talk about having a more traditional electric truck design if Cybertruck fails, but I doubt we will see that. Again, Elon is betting the house on autonomy.

title: Energica rises from the ashes with plans for cheaper electric motorcycles
content:
Electric Motorcycles
Energica
Micah Toll
| Nov 6 2026 - 1:50 am PT
Energica is officially back.
The Italian electric motorcycle maker,
which ceased operations in 2024
after entering judicial liquidation, has announced a major revival under new international ownership. And while the Energica name is returning, the company behind it is going to look quite different this time around.
Perhaps the biggest change is where the motorcycles will actually be built.
Energica
says motorcycle production is moving to Asia, while design, engineering, research and development, as well as responsibility for technical and quality standards, will remain in Italy. The new manufacturing setup is expected to significantly reduce production costs, allowing Energica to cut motorcycle prices by around 20% compared to its previous models.
That could be a big deal for a company whose motorcycles were widely praised for their performance and technology, but were also firmly positioned
at the premium end of the market.
The revival comes after Energica
was acquired by Energica Pte. Ltd.
, a Singapore-based company backed by international private investors. Importantly, much of the technological know-how isn’t disappearing overseas with the manufacturing. Energica says its core engineering and design leadership remains in Italy, including longtime CTO Giampiero Testoni and designer Paolo Imeni.
The first motorcycle to make its comeback will be the
Energica Experia
, the company’s adventure-oriented electric sport-tourer. After that, Energica plans to progressively restart production of the Ego, Eva Ribelle, and EsseEsse9, eventually bringing its entire previous lineup back to market.
At least initially, those motorcycles will use their existing platforms, which should help Energica get bikes rolling off the production line faster without having to develop and homologate entirely new machines. But upgrades are already planned, including a new battery and improvements to range, efficiency, performance, and reliability.
Energica is also specifically targeting Europe, the United States, and Australia as it rebuilds its dealer and service networks. Existing owners haven’t been forgotten either. The company says service has already resumed and spare-parts shipments have restarted to dealers in several countries.
For anyone who followed the electric motorcycle industry over the last decade, Energica’s disappearance was a particularly painful one. This wasn’t some startup with a couple of renderings and a dream. Energica built some of the highest-performance electric motorcycles on the road and spent four seasons supplying the motorcycles for the FIM MotoE World Cup, experience that helped develop its high-voltage and DC fast-charging technology.
Now the company gets something relatively rare in the motorcycle industry: a second chance.
And if moving production to Asia really can knock around 20% off Energica’s prices while retaining the Italian engineering that made the bikes special in the first place, Energica 2.0 might have a considerably better shot at turning great electric motorcycles into a sustainable business.
Electrek’s Take
It seems like moving toward Asian manufacturing is all but inevitable here. It was the expensive European manufacturing of low-volume motorcycles that weighed so heavily on Energica’s balance sheets in the years up to their financial troubles, and so shifting production to countries with both the expertise and the cost benefits for motorcycle manufacturing simply makes sense.
Energica isn’t alone in discovering the economics of moving electric motorcycle production to Asia. Zero Motorcycles spent years manufacturing its bikes in California before beginning a major shift toward production in the Philippines in 2023, including both complete motorcycles and major subassemblies. Now the company works with multiple factories, including major manufacturers like Zongshen in China, to reduce production costs for its electric motorcycles while still maintaining the ‘designed in California’ marketing angle.
It’s too early to tell how the new strategy will play out for Energica, but the fact that the company is now following a more well-worn trail is a positive sign for those who have spent the last two years hoping for a revival.

title: Sodium-ion batteries approach cost parity with LFP, with 70 GWh covered by supply agreements - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Sodium-ion batteries are approaching cell-level cost parity with LFP technology, with supply agreements exceeding 70 GWh worldwide. Despite higher upfront costs, they could offer a 21% lower total cost of ownership over 20 years, according to Wood Mackenzie.
Pilar Sánchez Molina
06 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Batteries
Energy Storage
Singeng sodium-ion battery project in Hubei
Sodium-ion battery technology is entering the commercial production phase and emerging as an alternative to lithium-ion batteries, driven by supply chain diversification, strong low-temperature performance, and the potential for lower total cost of ownership. According to an analysis by Wood Mackenzie, supply agreements totaling more than 70 GWh are already in place.
The study, which examines markets in China, the United States, Germany, and India, identifies sodium-ion batteries as the most promising emerging alternative to lithium-based technologies for stationary energy storage. Leading manufacturers are expected to achieve cell-level cost parity with lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries by late 2026, while parity at the module and system levels is not expected until after 2030.
China is leading the commercialization of the technology. BYD plans to reach 30 GWh of sodium-ion battery manufacturing capacity, while CATL aims to exceed 1 GWh in sodium-ion battery shipments by the end of 2026.
Supply agreements for sodium-ion batteries are already in place in China, the United States, and Europe, while India remains in the early stages of commercial validation. For the 2026–2035 period, Wood Mackenzie estimates a learning rate of 18% to 20% in China, reflecting the greater maturity of its industrial supply chain.
Planned manufacturing capacity currently exceeds demand, although the growing number of supply agreements points to the technology’s gradual adoption in the market.
Higher upfront costs, lower total cost of ownership
Sodium-ion batteries currently have higher upfront costs than LFP batteries. The global average stands at $229/kWh, compared with approximately $200/kWh for LFP batteries. However, Wood Mackenzie estimates that sodium-ion batteries could achieve a 21% lower total cost of ownership over a 20-year project lifetime.
The difference is primarily attributed to the elimination of capacity expansion cycles and lower operating costs. The economics of sodium-ion systems remain relatively stable across storage durations of two to four hours.
The study identifies raw material supply security, service life, and a wider operating temperature range as key technical advantages of sodium-ion batteries. The latter could make them particularly suitable for applications in cold climates, where lithium-ion batteries may require additional thermal management systems.
Regulation accelerates development
Industrial and trade policies are playing an increasingly important role in the competitiveness of different battery chemistries. In July 2026, China reintroduced a consumption tax on lithium-ion batteries while exempting sodium-ion batteries until the end of 2028. LFP batteries became subject to a 2% levy in September 2026, which is set to increase to 4% in September 2027.
In the United States, tariffs of approximately 58% on energy storage cells imported from China, combined with production tax credits under Section 45X of the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), are encouraging domestic sodium-ion battery manufacturing.
In Europe, carbon footprint declaration requirements under the EU Battery Regulation could favor technologies with supply chains that are less dependent on certain critical raw materials. Meanwhile, India is supporting domestic manufacturing through a $1.25 billion incentive program and tariff exemptions for certain types of manufacturing equipment.
Wood Mackenzie expects the 2030–2035 period to be decisive for sodium-ion batteries to achieve economic competitiveness. For energy storage projects currently under development, LFP remains the most commercially mature option for storage durations of two to four hours.

title: The Hydrogen Stream: H2 turbines can push LCOHS to around $0.62/kg - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Australian researchers found that hydrogen gas turbines could provide more cost-effective backup power than fuel cells during periods of low solar availability. Their study highlights how reservoir properties and system design affect the cost and performance of underground hydrogen storage.
Sergio Matalucci
06 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Energy Storage
Hydrogen
Utility-scale
Illustration of the large-scale underground hydrogen storage plant
Australian scientists
compared hydrogen fuel cells and hydrogen gas turbines as backup power sources during periods of low solar availability, finding that hydrogen turbines could offer lower capital expenditure and a levelized cost of hydrogen storage (LCOHS) of around AUD 0.90/kg ($0.62/kg) under modeled conditions of 10% porosity, 50 mD permeability, a 30-year project lifetime, and a 7% discount rate. “This paper demonstrates that the optimisation of integrated reservoir and surface systems could lower the LCOHS and enable the extensive implementation of solar-driven hydrogen production,” the researchers said in “
Feasibility assessment of solar-driven underground hydrogen storage through integrated surface and subsurface modelling
.” The paper, published in
Applied Energy
, assesses an integrated system encompassing hydrogen injection, geological storage, purification, and pipeline delivery. It highlights how reservoir characteristics affect hydrogen recovery and overall costs. Higher permeability improves injectivity and recovery rates but can increase purification and compression requirements, while lower porosity can improve gas displacement at the expense of higher injection pressures and equipment costs. The researchers said that interactions between reservoir properties and surface facility strategies are key to the performance of repurposed geological reservoirs for hydrogen storage, providing a basis for designing commercially viable, large-scale underground hydrogen storage (UHS) systems. Previous research has also examined
alternative approaches to hydrogen storage in lakes and reservoirs

reported significant charges related to business and asset restructuring, primarily associated with previously announced project exits. “During fiscal year 2026, we recorded pre-tax charges of approximately $3.2 billion ($2.4 billion attributable to Air Products after tax, or $10.95 per share). These charges primarily related to project exit actions announced on 30 June 2026, including the exit of a clean energy complex under construction in Louisiana, a green hydrogen production facility under construction in Casa Grande, Arizona, and certain other clean energy projects,” the Pennsylvania-based company said in its fiscal 2026 full-year results.
Everfuel
has signed a €245 million grant agreement with the German government to support its planned Project Frigg green hydrogen facility in Denmark. The funding, awarded through the European Hydrogen Bank’s Auctions-as-a-Service scheme, provides production support of €0.98/kg of renewable hydrogen. The Danish hydrogen developer has also reserved capacity in the Danish and German hydrogen pipeline networks equivalent to 400 MW of electrolyzer capacity. The project is designed to scale up to 2 GW of electrolyzer capacity as the market develops. Previous research has highlighted
Denmark’s potential role in European green hydrogen corridors
has awarded contracts for 11 new hydrogen-ready combined-cycle gas turbines (CCGTs), with a combined capacity of around 5.1 GW, under the Electricity Supply Security and Capacity Act (StromVKG). RWE secured contracts for 2.1 GW of capacity in the first long-term capacity auction. The Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur) is preparing a second auction, with the date scheduled to be announced on Nov. 10, 2026. The awards follow the
European Commission’s approval of Germany’s capacity mechanism
in September, which cleared the way for state support for new generation, storage, and demand-side flexibility, including hydrogen-ready gas-fired power plants.
Nippon Steel
has produced more than 1,000 metric tons of direct reduced iron (DRI) using 100% hydrogen as the reducing agent at its pilot-scale facility in Japan. The company completed more than 300 hours of continuous operation at its Hasaki Research and Development Center, using lower-grade iron ore pellets instead of the high-grade material typically required for direct reduction. The 60-meter-high furnace has a production capacity of 1 metric ton per hour and began operating in March 2026.
Asahi Kasei
Power to Hydrogen
(P2H2) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to evaluate the scale-up of manufacturing and commercialization of anion exchange membrane (AEM) water electrolysis systems. “Under the MOU, the companies will explore how to combine P2H2’s expertise in AEM electrolysis with Asahi Kasei’s broad capabilities developed across its existing electrolysis businesses within the next few years,” the Tokyo-based company said. P2H2 previously
completed a 1,250-hour pilot with Repsol
, demonstrating its hybrid AEM electrolysis technology under variable operating conditions. The company has also
deployed a 500 kW AEM electrolyzer at the Port of Antwerp-Bruges

The company will procure, install and maintain the computing equipment. The final contract value will depend on actual delivery volumes and agreed prices, and the maximum estimated amount does not constitute a revenue or earnings commitment. China’s National Energy Administration (NEA) published a proposed list of 93 pilot projects under its “AI+” energy initiative on Nov. 5, with a public consultation period running until Nov. 11. Of the total, 19 projects focus on emerging energy business models, including energy storage safety diagnostics, direct green power connections, coordinated power and computing operations, virtual power plants, and multi-energy system optimization. Participating technology providers include Sungrow, CATL and EVE Energy. The projects have passed expert evaluation and review but remain subject to public consultation. title: Soluxtec resumes TOPCon solar module production in Germany - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
The German solar module manufacturer has restarted production at its Trier-Föhren facility after upgrading its manufacturing lines to produce G12-format TOPCon modules. The company has yet to disclose the annual production capacity of the modernized plant.
Sandra Enkhardt
06 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
German solar module manufacturer
Soluxtec
has resumed production at its facility in Trier-Föhren, Germany, following its acquisition by Chinese PV manufacturer Ronmaa and a comprehensive upgrade of its existing production lines.
The company said it is now manufacturing solar modules based on tunnel oxide passivated contact (TOPCon) technology using G12-format cells, replacing the M10 format previously used at the facility. Soluxtec described the transition as “a core component of Soluxtec’s product and manufacturing strategy.”
Production will be ramped up gradually over the coming weeks, the company said without disclosing the annual production capacity of the modernized facility.
Soluxtec said its partnership with Romna will also support the expansion of its research and development activities. It added that its German manufacturing operations will provide a foundation for developing new PV products for residential and commercial and industrial (C&I) applications.
Soluxtec
filed for insolvency in April 2026
, citing intense international competition and declining solar module prices. The Bitburg District Court appointed Jakob Joeres of German auditing and consulting firm dhpg as provisional insolvency administrator. At the time, the company employed 70 people across its manufacturing operations in Bitburg and Föhren, where it had produced solar modules for 15 years.
Soluxtec’s management said at the time that it intended to maintain module deliveries, preserve jobs and seek investors to support a restructuring of the business.
The insolvency came amid sustained pressure on European solar manufacturers from low module prices and competition from overseas suppliers.
European TOPCon module prices fell sharply in 2024
, with weak demand and high inventories adding to the challenges facing manufacturers and distributors.

title: World's largest liquid-air storage facility comes online in China - pv magazine Global
content:
Applications & Installations
China’s 60 MW/600 MWh liquid-air energy storage facility in Qinghai began generating electricity on October 30, marking a major milestone in long-duration energy storage commercialization. The world’s largest grid-connected LAES project offers 10 hours of continuous power output, supporting renewable energy integration with domestically developed technology.
Vincent Shaw
06 Nov 2026
Applications & Installations
Energy Storage
Highlights
Qinghai Golmud 60MW Liquid Air Energy Storage National Demonstration Project
A 60 MW/600 MWh
liquid air energy storage
(LAES) demonstration project in Qinghai province, northwest China, was connected to the grid and began generating electricity on October 30, marking a significant step toward the commercial deployment of large-scale cryogenic energy storage.
Located in Golmud, Haixi Mongolian and Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, the facility was developed by state-owned China Green Development Investment Group (CGDG) in cooperation with the Technical Institute of Physics and Chemistry of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS).
The developer describes the project as the world’s largest grid-connected liquid-air energy storage facility by both rated power and energy capacity.
Construction began in July 2023. The project was selected for China’s national new-type energy storage demonstration program and included in the National Energy Administration’s list of major first-of-a-kind energy technologies and equipment.
With a rated output of 60 MW and a storage capacity of 600 MWh, the facility is designed to deliver electricity continuously for 10 hours. According to CGDG, it could accommodate approximately 600 MWh of surplus renewable electricity daily and supply an estimated 180 GWh to the grid annually, equivalent to the electricity consumption of around 30,000 households.
The system uses ambient air as its working fluid, avoiding the need for electrochemical batteries or underground storage caverns.
When charging, surplus electricity drives a three-stage centrifugal compressor, pressurizing purified air to approximately 7 MPa. Heat generated during compression is recovered and stored as hot water at temperatures reaching 195 C.
The compressed air then passes through a multistage cooling process before being liquefied at approximately -194 C and stored in insulated cryogenic tanks at near-atmospheric pressure.
During discharge, the liquid air is pressurized, reheated and vaporized. The expanding gas drives turbines connected to generators, while cold energy recovered during vaporization is stored for reuse in subsequent charging cycles.
The project incorporates several domestically developed technologies, including large centrifugal compressors, liquid expanders, cryogenic heat exchangers and integrated control systems. CGDG said all major equipment was manufactured domestically, achieving a 100% localization rate.
The technology was developed through collaboration between CGDG and CAS researchers, who previously demonstrated liquid-air energy storage at the 100-kW scale. Engineering design was undertaken by Hualu Engineering & Technology, with China National Chemical Engineering Third Construction participating in construction.
Unlike many compressed-air energy storage configurations that require suitable geological formations, liquid-air storage uses insulated tanks, allowing greater flexibility in site selection. The rotating machinery can also provide inertial support to the power grid, according to the project developer.
The facility is located in Qinghai’s renewable-rich Qaidam Basin, where long-duration storage could help shift surplus solar and wind generation to periods of higher electricity demand.
China is pursuing multiple long-duration energy storage technologies alongside its dominant lithium-ion battery industry. Compressed-air systems, vanadium redox flow batteries, sodium-ion batteries and thermal storage are being developed for different operating durations and grid applications. The latest Golmud project provides a large-scale engineering demonstration for liquid-air storage.

title: S-5! presents height-adjustable mounting system for PV modules on metal roofs - pv magazine Global
content:
Technology & Products
S-5! has introduced the PVKIT 3.0, a rail-less mounting system for solar panels on metal roofs, available with an optional 50 mm clearance for wiring and power electronics. The system features non-penetrating attachments and accommodates PV module frames ranging from 25 mm to 35 mm, depending on the configuration.
François Puthod
06 Nov 2026
Technology & Products
Commercial & industrial
Residential
The PVKIT 3.0 is available in a standard configuration or with an integrated 50 mm clearance.
Rooftop solar installations increasingly incorporate power optimizers, microinverters and other components that require additional space beneath the modules.
Developed by S-5!, the PVKIT 3.0 mounting solution addresses this need by providing additional clearance for cable routing, module-level power electronics (MLPE) and access to wiring. The standard configuration allows modules to be installed closer to the roof surface when additional clearance is not required.
“The PVKIT 3.0 was designed to give designers and installers greater control over the gap between the roof and the solar panels,” said Rob Haddock, CEO and founder of S-5!. “The choice between a standard configuration and an integrated 50 mm clearance makes it easier to accommodate various wiring, electronic component, and related equipment needs—all while maintaining the simplicity of a rail-less mounting system.”
Backed by a lifetime warranty, the PVKIT 3.0 works with S-5! clamps and brackets to form a complete DirectAttach mounting system for metal roofs. On standing-seam and concealed-fastener roofs, the system provides non-penetrating attachment without compromising roof integrity, according to the manufacturer.
The standard configuration is compatible with PV modules featuring frame thicknesses of 28 mm to 35 mm, while the integrated clearance option accommodates frames ranging from 25 mm to 35 mm.
According to S-5!, the PVKIT 3.0 reduces mounting system weight, volume and carbon footprint by up to 85% compared with conventional rail-based systems, while requiring significantly fewer components. The company also claims a 25% reduction in load distribution, with the rail-less design eliminating the need for on-site rail cutting, potentially reducing transportation and logistics costs.
The PVKIT 3.0 comes pre-assembled and can be installed using a single tool, reducing the number of components and hardware that installers need to transport, organize and handle on the roof.
Stainless steel grounding teeth provide electrical continuity and grounding between PV module frames. The system also features corrosion-resistant components designed for long-term performance under demanding rooftop conditions.
